⚡ The Signal

Two of the biggest AI labs spent the same day teaching their assistants to listen.

Dear Readers,

On July 23, OpenAI and Anthropic both shipped voice upgrades within hours of each other, and the timing matters. OpenAI pushed its full-duplex GPT-Live model into the ChatGPT desktop app and Codex, so engineers can steer coding jobs without touching the keyboard. Anthropic moved Claude's voice mode onto its stronger models and let it reach the tools you have already connected, from Gmail to Notion. Voice is turning from a party trick into the control layer for real work, which sharpens an old question: once talking is the fastest way to run software, who is really steering?

🩺 ChatGPT Wants to Read Your Medical Records

OpenAI just handed ChatGPT the keys to your medical file. Health in ChatGPT is now live for every logged-in US user over 18, on the free, Go, Plus, and Pro tiers. It links Apple Health and records from providers like Epic and Oracle Health, then answers questions about labs, medications, and sleep in plain language. OpenAI says it already fields 300 million health questions a week, and warns the tool is "not intended for use in the diagnosis or treatment of any health condition."

👉 tl;dr: Real convenience meets your most sensitive data, and the privacy trade-off is now everyone's.

📉 Oracle's AI Bet Costs 21,000 Jobs

Oracle is cutting about 21,000 jobs, roughly 13% of staff, even as it goes all-in on AI. Headcount falls from around 162,000 to 141,000 while the firm funds a reported $300 billion compute deal with OpenAI. A credit downgrade from BBB to BBB- has triggered fresh collateral demands, including a $7 billion guarantee sought by Wisconsin regulators for a data center.

👉 tl;dr: The AI boom's backbone is brutally expensive, and Oracle is trimming people to pay for machines.

🤖 The US Moves to Keep Chinese Robots Out of the Military

Congress wants Chinese humanoid robots nowhere near the US military. A provision in the House-passed NDAA would bar the Pentagon from buying, leasing, or operating humanoid robots made by "foreign adversaries" including China, Russia, and Iran. It is far narrower than the sweeping GUARD Act floated last year by Representative John Moolenaar: commercial sales to US businesses and consumers stay untouched, for now.

👉 tl;dr: Washington's first hard line on physical AI starts at the barracks door.

Two Labs, One Day: Voice Becomes How You Run Your AI

The Takeaway

👉 On July 23, OpenAI brought its full-duplex GPT-Live voice model to the ChatGPT desktop app and Codex, so you can dictate, steer, and debug coding jobs hands-free.

👉 The same day, Anthropic upgraded Claude's voice mode to run on Opus and Sonnet, up from the small Haiku model, and to reach connected apps like Gmail and Notion mid-conversation.

👉 Both push voice past dictation into a control layer: you run software and orchestrate agents by speaking, the way you would brief a colleague.

👉 The catch: Anthropic left its underlying voice model untouched, so latency still trails OpenAI, and hands-free tool access raises real oversight questions.

For three years, using an AI assistant mostly meant typing at it and waiting your turn. This week, two of the biggest labs decided that was the slow way to work.

On July 23, OpenAI extended GPT-Live, the full-duplex model it launched July 8 that can listen and speak at once, into the ChatGPT desktop app on macOS and Windows, wired straight into Codex, its coding agent, and ChatGPT Work. In one demo, two engineers spoke to the same session in the same room, each giving separate instructions while the model kept working. The pitch is hands-free agentic coding: you start jobs, review pull requests, and debug by talking, while the model hands the heavy reasoning to GPT-5.5 in the background.

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80,width=1920,height=3840/uploads/asset/file/77721116-22bc-4fce-a438-cd97739ba32b/Image_Aspect_Ratio__32_.png?t=1784914627> 	
(OpenAI CEO Sam Altman / Getty Images via Fortune) 

Almost at the same time, Anthropic shipped its own upgrade. Claude's voice mode, once stuck on the small Haiku model, can now run on Opus or Sonnet and talk problems through in ten languages. More important, voice reaches the tools you have already connected, Gmail, Google Calendar, Slack, Canva, and Notion, so you can reschedule a meeting or draft a document by speaking. Free users get Haiku and one app; paid plans unlock the rest.

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80,width=1920,height=3840/uploads/asset/file/ba3c7148-c140-4422-ae85-2d6402df1487/Image_Aspect_Ratio__33_.png?t=1784914634> 	
(Claude voice mode / Anthropic via TechCrunch) 

The symmetry is the story: two rivals, same day, moved voice from a novelty you demo once into the layer you use to operate the machine. They took different roads: Anthropic admits it did not change its underlying voice model, so its latency still feels clumsier than OpenAI's continuous audio. And giving a talkative agent live access to your inbox and codebase is convenient right up until it does the wrong thing fast. The quicker you can tell software what to do, the quicker a misheard instruction becomes an action you never wanted.

Why it matters: When talking becomes the fastest way to run your tools and your code, the interface stops being something you look at and becomes something you converse with. That shifts who does the typing, and it puts a premium on the machine hearing you right.

The chart: Oracle's stock over the last six months, the other half of the layoffs story. Shares closed at $120.04 on July 23, down about 34% in six months after peaking near $250 in early summer. A 2% after-hours bounce barely dented the slide.

The lesson: Wall Street has soured on the pay-now, earn-later math of the AI infrastructure race. Oracle staked its future on a reported $300 billion compute commitment to OpenAI and a wave of data centers; investors have roughly halved the value they briefly gave that bet.

The caveat: One stock is not the whole trade. Oracle carries its own baggage, from collateral demands to heavy debt, so the drop is partly company-specific. Still, it is a clear warning that the market will punish the gap between huge outlays and revenue that has not arrived.

⚖️ Europe Fines First, Builds Later

⚡ Bottom line: On August 2 the EU AI Act starts handing regulators the power to fine AI providers up to €35M or 7% of global revenue.

💡 Why it matters: Any company serving EU users now carries the compliance load, even as Brussels delays the law's hardest parts.

🔎 What it means: Europe is quick to regulate and slow to build, and that gap is becoming its defining AI problem.

On August 2, the European Union starts writing fines. That is when the EU AI Act, the world's first comprehensive AI law, hands regulators real enforcement power over providers of general-purpose AI models, the systems behind ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. The penalties are steep: up to €35 million or 7% of worldwide revenue, a ceiling above the GDPR's, and every one of the 27 member states has to stand up its own AI regulator.

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80,width=1920,height=3840/uploads/asset/file/37c06863-83b6-4666-b9bc-8a000d90c9d4/Image_Aspect_Ratio__34_.png?t=1784914743> 	
(The EU Artificial Intelligence Act)

What actually arrives is transparency paperwork. Under Article 50, chatbots must announce they are machines, and AI-generated images, audio, and video must be labelled as synthetic. Useful in theory, though it lands the same week Black Forest Labs shows off a model that spins up video, audio, and action in one shot, a reminder of how far the tech has run ahead of the rules.

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80,width=1920,height=3840/uploads/asset/file/3979f26c-61f7-4bfc-a557-ea9f3f411951/Outline__21_.png?t=1784914756> 	
(European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen)

The awkward part is what Brussels quietly dropped. A late amendment, the Digital Omnibus, has pushed the heavier high-risk rules, covering hiring, education, and biometrics, more than a year down the road to late 2027, after industry and Washington complained. So Europe gets the fines and the forms now and the substance later, all while it struggles to field a single frontier lab of its own. Writing the rulebook was never the hard part; building something worth regulating is.

Switching wireless providers is now stress-free with our end-to-end transition service

 

It hasnʼt been easy for larger businesses to transition to a new wireless provider. Until now. Introducing AT&T Switch Assist, a complimentary white-glove service that helps you seamlessly transition the devices of multiple employees. So, when youʼre ready to upgrade your wireless, weʼll take care of everything.

 
Learn more <https://app.responses.att-mail.com/e/er?s=1981585949&lid=16909&elqTrackId=999fed58267d48248fefa1b5a8f22235&eloqua_cid=CATEL000094804085&elq=f86c36c7df6447979d799e36b410c197&elqaid=39893&elqat=1&elqak=8AF5754E45100FF77AAD0A08168BFD1A9DDF183839F33889353A533EB8A2F53E3810>

Includes a detailed transition plan tailored to your specific business needs.

Every step meticulously handled from end to end, to minimize disruption.

Dedicated virtual project manager oversees the entire process.

No cost to you, starting on orders for as few as 20 smartphone lines.

 
Learn more <https://app.responses.att-mail.com/e/er?s=1981585949&lid=16908&elqTrackId=408cbec7ec154d28a070d44e1bb8b1b5&eloqua_cid=CATEL000094804085&elq=f86c36c7df6447979d799e36b410c197&elqaid=39893&elqat=1&elqak=8AF5EA9B1B3DB8A928AAA0037E6A0AD62A3E183839F33889353A533EB8A2F53E3810>  	
 
 

Get up to $50,000 when you break free

 

Learn how to get up to $450* per line when you switch your wireless to AT&T

 

Requires port-in of new line(s) on elig. AT&T wireless service for business. Payment based on remaining balance or termination fee on your non-AT&T wireless smartphone line(s) (up to $450/line, up to $50,000/business). Submit most recent bill(s) within 60 days of activation. Fees & other charges, terms & restr’s. apply. See offer details below.

 
 <https://contenthub.att.com/transform/To_PNG/4f828708-37dc-463f-a3cb-ce0caf068899/7047621-Secondary-Offer-Image> 
 
 

To speak to an AT&T Business advisor about this exclusive offer:

 
Call 844.784.0200 <tel:8447840200>  	
 
 
 <https://contenthub.att.com/transform/To_PNG/03d97fef-a741-4874-94f8-d79b4753dd1e/AT-T-Guarantee-Blue-Bg-DT> 
 <https://contenthub.att.com/transform/To_PNG/b98e2410-2842-4a48-8158-a10d1a5948e1/AT-T-Guarantee-Blue-Bg-MOB> 
 

Get backed by the AT&T Guarantee®

 

Connectivity you depend on. Deals you want. Prompt, friendly service you deserve. All guaranteed, or we make it right.

 

Learn more at att.com/businessguarantee <https://app.responses.att-mail.com/e/er?s=1981585949&lid=16907&elqTrackId=9fe9d9d71cd14f4c824043e527902939&eloqua_cid=CATEL000094804085&elq=f86c36c7df6447979d799e36b410c197&elqaid=39893&elqat=1&elqak=8AF5F8568F838C2792C0404D4D866C2A973B183839F33889353A533EB8A2F53E3810> 

 
 <https://contenthub.att.com/transform/59a50543-a5c3-425c-b06c-1d4c1f464d6c/ATTBusiness_White_Logo?io=transform:trim,padding:2&io=transform:fill,width:312&format=png> 
 

*$450/LINE SWITCHER OFFER: Subject to change. Eligibility: Avail. only to business customers with a qual. wireless svc. agrmt. (Business Agrmt.) for Corporate Responsibility User (CRU) lines of service.  Business customers who were active and in good standing with an eligible competing wireless provider are eligible for up to $450/line (“Payout”) if they meet all requirements. Payout requires (1) an amount owed (unpaid smartphone installment plan balance [“Payoff”] and/or early termination fee [“ETF”]) to a U.S. wireless service provider other than AT&T (“Third-Party Provider”) on a smartphone line; (2) port-in of that same phone number line from the Third-Party Provider to AT&T; (3) activation of that phone number on a qualifying AT&T postpaid wireless line of svc. (voice & data) for business. Eligible business customer must meet these three requirements for a minimum of 11 lines. Customer may purchase a new smartphone from AT&T or bring an already-owned compatible smartphone. Customer is responsible for completing any device unlock, installment plan balance payoff, and any other process or payment required by the Third-Party Provider prior to porting a line. Eligible Wireless: AT&T Business Preferred E Advanced ($35/mo.), AT&T Business Preferred E Premium ($40/mo.), AT&T Business Preferred E Premium with Turbo ($55/mo.), AT&T Business E Advanced B ($45/mo.). (Preferred Plans: Not eligible for AutoPay or paperless bill discount. Add $10/mo. if device is activated on a 2- or 3-yr. contract.) Prices exclude taxes and fees. Final plan pricing, features, terms, and restrictions may vary based on customer size, contract length, and other factors. Switcher Payout: Payout to a business customer will be determined by the balance on the Third-Party Provider smartphone line (Payoff or ETF) and will not exceed $450 per line or $50,000 per business. Payout will not be made for any charges or fees other than Payoff or ETF. To receive Payout for a given line, the line must remain active on a qualifying AT&T wireless plan for a minimum of 30 days from activation. Activation date starts same day as AT&T Installment Plan℠ or service agreement. To receive Payout for a line, the business customer must upload the most recent Third-Party Provider customer bill showing then-current Payoff or ETF, dated no more than three calendar months prior to AT&T service activation date. Bill must be uploaded to rewardcenteroffers.com/BusinessPayoff <https://app.responses.att-mail.com/e/er?s=1981585949&lid=16906&elqTrackId=424204d8c11d4670b763d86b3b433af5&eloqua_cid=CATEL000094804085&elq=f86c36c7df6447979d799e36b410c197&elqaid=39893&elqat=1&elqak=8AF57E72C65A1D90EF8E8143A744E4D38374183839F33889353A533EB8A2F53E3810>  within 60 days of first AT&T line activation under this offer. To receive Payout for a line, the line must be ported to AT&T within 90 days of activation of the business customer’s first line ported under this offer. Payout for all offer-eligible lines from a business customer will be made by up to four checks sent on or about day 45, day 60, day 90, and day 120 after first eligible activation and bill upload under this offer. Checks may take up to 10 business days to arrive. Limits: Third-Party Provider eligibility excludes Cricket, AT&T Prepaid®, AT&T Resellers, Residential Wireless, Wireline VoIP services. Some Third-Party Provider phone features may not work on the AT&T network. Offer may not be combinable w/ other offers, discounts, or credits. Purchase, financing, other limits & restr’s. apply. This offer may make your account ineligible for select other offers (including bill credit offers) for 12 months. Talk to your AT&T representative for more details. GEN. WIRELESS SVC.: Subj. to applicable Business Agrmt. (see your AT&T representative for terms) and credit approval. Pricing, promotions, terms, and restrictions may be modified or terminated at any time without notice.

What Actually Escaped in July, and What Only Looked Like It 


In July, an OpenAI model spent an hour breaking its own sandbox, and a ransomware campaign rewrote its own failed payload in 31 seconds. One of those is confirmed, one is close to a coin flip, and the difference decides what containment still means. 

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/guest_author/profile_picture/c5566308-189f-41ea-9af4-16cb3059e723/thumb_RW7VBJfD_400x400.jpg> 	 	Kim "Chubby" Isenberg <https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/OnwjrOHobTjxkYjcw6tdI3e79E%2FWGESl3mzqZ18M5ZXQrpBGX0ZBCpDTrHdB%0Ak1NBzHaoG70IPIkLy0k1PGO9xGD5%2F9egiCI7%2BMtmIaLMl5KY3E72FuviJD%2BM%0AHEJweIR4UGbQZKkqIc%2FJbx75qCrisl6m9%2FnibH9dapYsxLlNo1O%2F%2Bfcxr8%2Fp%0AJwAobtdTOJpdQbjDAh0%2BE2l%2BfivceQ3hxw%3D%3D%0A/bed1e0f0971d47ed> 

 <https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/o/AT6FUaCAgDGWpFCAdMdWM5azuxu%2BcU2vEUGoodal4fLIHXS0Llfb3UCVDab6%0AriPtRLrbvGWmNdCI6BcKPgKqYDMrqxQatIkuNBb8vlVn%2BxQ%2BfABNEWsNU6ZH%0ABPxokXYXs5WZZWyDiN0JU5CSkmrpeKCx8Xsfg0%2Bd3Yr8mt6QjexidAgisKDW%0AzsCNvLSyN4%2F2cDPuG5gZduYOGdsLEK7YpRxcZeNTZ5Wk1BoOTJJvsaV1B9lx%0AzPtXLTMZBER3LamHDCvZg9NGdCawe0GXHX65vOPW9GGrr5CpNpGHHZ%2F5Gshp%0A2Iw0fPUtJnBUMQOgIoHZWCrrAc92G2XZN8CwEfFWA6qsl87jpArwXnP1nFMx%0AmKbJMnbreERebOGZf02w0VVDU5gzuiTLL61dZDJwnpKkR6KKsDbcD%2BofpI5Z%0ADPXo7AdPBGB5FzF1djhB3f8ovkTUG61zyIiQt5fb%2F0nxnlTBCg%3D%3D%0A/d31ac0b155fddf63.gif> 
  	In Today’s Issue:

⏱️ The hour and the 31 seconds, and what the two events have in common

🏷️ Three classes of claim, and why this issue sorts every fact into one

🔓 What OpenAI actually disclosed, including the incidents after redeployment

🤖 The 55 out of 100, and the case that JADEPUFFER had no AI in it at all

💰 Why the containment question that has an answer is about cost, not escape

  	
A note from us: University students receive our Saturday Deepdive for free when they register with their university email address at: https://getsuperintel.com/plus-whitelist <https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/mUqPJCpEgU%2BMBMOPL4swzDc3M0QCwAIiPXD7G5gjeBa0nPSG6syAQoyRkwit%0AssOEDkoNxmcRnnGC6dkh04g3B%2FvnfEBiB1KfhxrODa9VfxHWz9hqh2VGDj70%0A%2BLw5Saz%2Bx%2Fu9kfZeuIVpV1TlT7tfa1MYe9NbFbqD6wzfRdXPQhODUu5PhgHx%0AkjdTcRbXpdPuLI5zTvJeyMlYHPSiCGfFbg%3D%3D%0A/18f5d53aeb3e5c61> 

  	
Dear Readers,

At 19:34:36 UTC, somewhere near the turn from June to July, something logged into an internet-facing Langflow server and failed. Thirty-one seconds later, at 19:35:07, without any human touching a keyboard in between, a corrected payload went in and worked, after two candidate explanations for the failure had been tested side by side (Sysdig, 07/01/2026). Over the hours that followed, the operation ran more than six hundred distinct, purposeful payloads, encrypted 1,342 database configuration items, and left a ransom note claiming a grade of encryption it had not actually used. Nineteen days later, a company with an entirely different problem published an entirely different kind of admission.

On 07/20/2026, OpenAI wrote that one of its internal, unreleased models had spent about an hour finding a vulnerability in its own sandbox so it could finish a task the way it judged the task should be finished, rather than the way it had been instructed (OpenAI, 07/20/2026). The model had developed a learning-rate technique during a training benchmark and wanted to publish it where that community publishes results, on a public GitHub leaderboard, even though its instructions said to report only in Slack. It hit a wall built specifically to stop it, and instead of stopping, it took the wall apart.

Before anything else, the deflation. No model escaped onto the open internet, none acted with full autonomy in the wild, and none evaded human oversight. The OpenAI incident happened inside an access-controlled environment the company built and watched, and the company paused internal deployment once the behavior surfaced (OpenAI, 07/20/2026). The ransomware campaign, which its investigators named JADEPUFFER, ran against a single misconfigured server carrying a publicly documented vulnerability that had been patchable for more than a year (Sysdig, 07/01/2026; Horizon3, 04/09/2025). What happened in July is smaller than the headlines and stranger than the summaries.

The strangeness sits in how differently the two stories are known. One is a detailed self-report by the company that owns the model, with no external auditor anywhere in the account. The other is a forensic reconstruction by one security vendor of one customer's compromised machine, and the question of whether an AI was making the decisions at all has been scored, by the sharpest published critique of that report, at 55 out of 100 (Ganiere, 07/05/2026). Both got covered as if they were the same class of fact, and sorting them is the whole exercise.

So the question this piece holds is narrower than the one the coverage asked, and harder to dodge. In July, two disclosures described the same behavior, a system that does not stop at an obstacle. How much of that is actually established, and what does the honest answer change about who can still control an AI system once it is running?


All the best,

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80,width=1920,height=3840/uploads/asset/file/c82900b7-ebbf-4eb6-811f-86a9b3dac911/image.png?t=1756137355> 	
Kim Isenberg

  	
  	

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80,width=1920,height=3840/uploads/asset/file/a98a2d23-c1c1-4275-864b-62473208566e/Export_Line_03.png?t=1760718394> 	
  	
One Confirmed Case, One Coin Flip, and a Hole That Sat Open for a Year


Three classes of claim

Almost every argument about July collapses if you read all its facts at the same volume, so this piece keeps three settings apart, and every claim below carries its setting with it.

The first is confirmed and independent, which means at least two parties with no shared interest describe the same thing, or a fact is checkable by anyone who wants to check it. The second is self-report, which means a party involved in the event is the only source for it, whether that party is a frontier lab describing its own model or a security vendor describing its own customer's server. Self-report is not a synonym for false, and the detail in both July disclosures is far richer than a company protecting itself would volunteer. It does mean nobody outside the reporting party has verified a word of it. The third is assessment, which means someone read the evidence and drew a conclusion from it, including the reporting parties themselves. Sysdig's own language is careful here in a way most of the coverage was not.

 <https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80,width=1920,height=3840/uploads/asset/file/6e29d195-51e8-49b1-b1bf-79a66d3a61f5/Outline__22_.png?t=1785001897> 	
Seven core claims from both incidents, sorted by how each one is actually evidenced. Only three of the seven survive as confirmed and independent. (Source: Superintelligence analysis; underlying sources OpenAI, Kalai, GitHub PR #300, Zvi Mowshowitz, Sysdig, Horizon3, Project Overwatch) 

Read that way, the July record thins out considerably. Three claims are genuinely confirmed by independent parties: the mathematical result behind OpenAI's model, the credit chain that proves the model's technique propagated to a third party, and the age of the vulnerability that let the ransomware in. Everything that made the headlines sits in the other two columns.

Subject: RE: Chick-fil-A & AZP Monument Sign Review (06/10/26)

 

Steve, Rocky,

 

In case we don’t talk today, here is the summary.

 

Planning has been approached by all parties for this signage proposal, and they have stated several times that no individual tenant signage will be considered, only the multi-tenant signs that match the new remodeled versions (8’ max height).

 

We can approve 2 new multi-tenant signs in that span. Starting from the larger 14’ sign in between the carwash and Wendy’s, and moving west, we can do a new sign every 275’ (min), as there is exactly room for 2.

 

These signs must be approved and permitted as duplicates of the existing signs, BUT…..The tenant panels can be manipulated per the discretion of the PM to accommodate individual tenants requests. For example, the sign must be approved with 5 max panels per side, but if the PM wanted to allow one tenant, usually like a major or anchor tenant, to utilize the space or total area of 2 or 3 panels, then they can allow this. So then you would have the same sign and sign panel area but with one large panel and 2 smaller ones. Just an example. The only requirements are that the panel background colors must meet the sign criteria (white), no corporate-colored panels, only corporate colored copy and graphics…ROUTED AND PUSH-THRU.

 

I hope this makes sense! Except for being away from my desk occasionally, I am here until 4:50 today and back in tomorrow at 8am.

 

Thank you!

Hi Joe,

We are looking for some guidance regarding a proposed monument sign arrangement within the Desert Palms development at Alma School Road and Warner Road.


Attached is a site plan showing the proposed locations of:

• One Chick-fil-A monument sign
• One AZP multi-tenant monument sign


Based on the plan, the two proposed signs appear to be separated by approximately 302 feet. While this appears to satisfy the typical monument sign separation requirement, we are unsure whether the site's PAD zoning, Master Sign Program, or previously approved sign package would permit this arrangement.

A separate Chick-fil-A monument sign and a separate AZP multi-tenant monument sign located approximately 302 feet apart within the same overall development.

Hi Rocky,

I reviewed the Chandler Sign Code along with the site plan provided.


Based on the plan, the proposed Chick-fil-A monument sign and the AZP multi-tenant monument sign appear to be separated by approximately 302 feet, which would satisfy the 300-foot separation requirement typically applied to freestanding monument signs within commercial centers.


However, the primary issue does not appear to be the separation distance itself. The larger consideration is whether the site's PAD zoning and any previously approved sign package or Master Sign Program would permit the additional monument sign arrangement. The Chandler Sign Code indicates that PAD developments may be governed by previously approved sign criteria that can supersede the standard code provisions.


Because of this, I would not consider the layout automatically approved based solely on the Sign Code. The proposal appears supportable from a spacing standpoint, but final determination should come from the Planning Department after reviewing the parcel configuration, ownership structure, PAD approvals, and existing sign program for the site.


My recommendation is that we contact Chandler Planning and request confirmation that the proposed arrangement of a separate Chick-fil-A monument sign and a separate AZP multi-tenant monument sign would be acceptable under the current PAD approvals.


Please let me know if you would like me to reach out to the city and obtain their interpretation.

subject: FW: Chick-fil-A & AZP Monument Sign Review (06/10/26)
body:
Hi Joe,



I hope you are doing well.


We are looking for some guidance regarding a proposed monument sign arrangement within the Desert Palms development at Alma School Road and Warner Road.


Attached is a site plan showing the proposed locations of:

• One Chick-fil-A monument sign
• One AZP multi-tenant monument sign


Based on the plan, the two proposed signs appear to be separated by approximately 302 feet. While this appears to satisfy the typical monument sign separation requirement, we are unsure whether the site's PAD zoning, Master Sign Program, or previously approved sign package would permit this arrangement.


Specifically, we are trying to determine whether Chandler would support:


A separate Chick-fil-A monument sign and a separate AZP multi-tenant monument sign located approximately 302 feet apart within the same overall development.


The parcels are anticipated to be separately owned, and we would appreciate any insight you can provide regarding whether this concept appears supportable or if Planning review would be required before moving forward.


Thank you for your time and assistance. Any guidance you can provide would be greatly appreciated.

subject: Conax Technologies Sign Proposal and Artwork Options (06/08/26)
body:
Hi Shannon,



Thank you for the opportunity to provide a proposal for the new Conax Technologies building signage.


Attached are our estimate and artwork concept options for your review. The proposed sign consists of a new internally illuminated pan channel letter sign featuring the Conax Technologies logo and copy, designed to complement the building while providing excellent visibility and nighttime illumination.


We have included two artwork options for consideration. Both concepts utilize illuminated pan channel letters with white LED illumination and non-illuminated "Technologies" copy. The options differ slightly in overall appearance and letter treatment, allowing you to select the version that best fits your branding preferences.


Our proposal includes:

• Fabrication and installation of one new internally illuminated pan channel letter sign
• Permit acquisition services
• Estimated City of Tempe permit fees
• Standard electrical connection to the existing sign circuit


Please review the attached artwork and proposal and let us know which option you prefer, or if you would like any revisions for consideration. We would be happy to make adjustments and provide updated artwork as needed.


If you have any questions, please feel free to contact me.

subject: Habit Burger # 65027 (27782) – Glendale Correction Comments (06/05/26)
body:
Hi Taylor,



Attached are the City of Glendale correction comments and redlined plans for the Habit Burger project.


Please review and revise the drawings accordingly. The primary comments are summarized below:



Planning Comments

1. Property Line / Right-of-Way

*         The property line must be clearly shown on the site plan.

*         The city notes that no signs may be located within the public right-of-way.

2. Building Sign Area

*         The city has determined that the building sign allowance is based on the available business frontage.

*         The submitted building sign is shown at approximately 26.62 square feet, while the reviewer indicates an allowable area of approximately 16.4 square feet based on the frontage shown.

*         Please review and revise the sign size or provide any supporting information necessary to demonstrate compliance.

3. Drive-Thru Sign Height

*         The city requires the exact height from finished grade to the top of the drive-thru sign.

*         Per Glendale Code Section 35.4.310(E)(2)(b), drive-thru signs are limited to 64 square feet in area and 6 feet in height.

*         The reviewer has requested that the sign height be reduced to comply with the ordinance.



Structural Comments

4. Arizona-Sealed Engineering

*         The city is requiring drawings and calculations sealed by an Arizona-registered engineer for the overhead sign structures and associated foundations.

5. Foundation Coordination

*         Several foundation details require clarification.

*         The reviewer noted that certain dimensions do not match between sheets and that some foundation details are not clearly associated with a specific sign.

*         Please coordinate the foundation drawings and clearly identify which sign each foundation detail applies to.

6. Structural Information

*         Additional column, frame, foundation, and connection information is required for review and approval.


Please provide revised drawings, Arizona-sealed engineering (as required), and a written response letter addressing each comment so we can prepare the resubmittal package.


Let me know if you have any questions regarding the City's comments.


Thank you,

 

Steve Skye

subject: 51 Bells Road Property – Glendale CSP Review (06/05/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,



I spoke with Alex Lerma, Planner for the City of Glendale, regarding the Comprehensive Sign Program (CSP) for the 51 Bells Road property.


The City's position is that the existing CSP no longer adequately reflects the current configuration of the property. Specifically, the south parcel (APN 200-50-013C) does not appear to be clearly addressed within the existing CSP, creating ambiguity regarding sign rights, allocations, and future sign approvals.


Alex indicated that Glendale would prefer to amend the existing CSP rather than establish an entirely new sign program. However, based on the extent of the revisions needed, the amendment would likely function as a substantial rewrite of the document.


The recommendation is to revise the CSP to incorporate both parcels, update the legal descriptions and exhibits, and establish clear sign criteria applicable to the property as it exists today. Glendale staff also suggested that the revised CSP be written comprehensively enough to maximize the sign allowances permitted under the current Glendale Sign Code, rather than remaining constrained by the limitations of the older CSP.


Based on the discussion, the opportunity exists to create a more robust and modern sign program that clearly addresses both parcels and provides greater flexibility for future tenant and property signage needs.


I've attached a summary of my discussion with Glendale Planning for your review.


Please let me know if you would like to discuss further.


Best,

We are pleased to report that fabrication of the reverse channel letters is now substantially complete. The letter cans have been assembled, welded, and fitted, and the project has progressed into the finishing and illumination phases.


As shown in the attached photos:

*	The fabricated letter cans are complete and ready for surface preparation and paint. 
*	The clear polycarbonate backs have been fabricated and fitted with mounting hardware. 
*	LED illumination modules are currently being assembled and installed onto the backing panels.

Over the next several days, the letters will move through:

*	Final surface preparation

body:
Hi Daryl,



Thank you for the opportunity to provide a proposal for the new signage at Subcity Restaurant Sports Lounge.


Attached please find our estimate and concept artwork for your review. The proposal includes:

• New internally illuminated channel letter display for the building façade
• New illuminated logo cabinet for the building exterior
• New graphic panels for the existing freestanding sign
• New reader board panels and copy area updates
• LED retrofit of the existing freestanding sign cabinets to improve illumination, efficiency, and long-term maintenance performance


The proposed design is intended to create a strong visual presence for the restaurant while providing improved visibility both during the day and at night. The building signage and freestanding sign graphics have been designed to establish a consistent brand identity throughout the property.

subject: Chandler Fashion Center – Contract Review Observations (06/01/26)
body:
Hi Wendy,



I reviewed the Macerich Construction Services Agreement for the Chandler Fashion Center freeway pylon project and wanted to provide a summary of several provisions that may warrant additional review prior to execution.


The primary items that stood out are as follows:



• Payment Terms
The agreement does not appear to follow the 50% / 50% payment structure shown on our estimate. Instead, payments are based on monthly progress billings, with the Owner retaining 10% of approved billings until final completion and closeout. This may have a significant impact on project cash flow, particularly during engineering, permitting, material procurement, and fabrication.



• Retention
The agreement provides for a 10% retention on progress payments. Based on the current contract value, this could result in approximately $40,000 being withheld until final completion and acceptance.



• Final Payment Requirements
Final payment is contingent upon completion of all work, punch list items, governmental approvals, warranties, lien releases, as-built drawings, and other closeout documentation. The agreement also allows additional time for processing final payment after these requirements have been satisfied.



• Fixed Price Contract
The agreement identifies the contract amount as a fixed and firm price. Material cost increases, labor escalation, and other market fluctuations do not appear to be grounds for price adjustment unless addressed through an approved change order.



• Change Orders
The agreement requires written authorization for changes affecting cost or schedule. Work performed outside the original scope without proper written approval may not be compensable.



• Permits, Inspections, and Governmental Fees
The agreement places responsibility for permits, inspections, licenses, and related approvals upon the contractor unless otherwise stated. Our proposal currently identifies City permit fees as additional costs billed at actual cost, and this item may warrant clarification.



• Indemnification / Hold Harmless
The agreement contains broad indemnification and hold harmless provisions requiring Christy Signs to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Macerich and various affiliated entities from claims, damages, losses, expenses, and attorney's fees arising from our work to the extent caused by Christy Signs or its subcontractors. These obligations survive project completion and represent one of the more significant risk-allocation provisions within the agreement.



• Mechanic's Liens and Claims
The agreement also requires the contractor to promptly address mechanic's liens or similar claims and may require reimbursement of related legal expenses and costs incurred by the Owner.



• Schedule Requirements
The agreement places significant emphasis on schedule compliance and completion deadlines. Delays and schedule modifications generally require formal documentation and approval.



• As-Built Documentation
The contractor is responsible for maintaining and providing complete as-built drawings and project closeout documentation as a condition of final payment.


Overall, the provisions that appear most significant from a project management and financial standpoint are the payment structure, retention requirements, fixed-price language, indemnification obligations, and contractor responsibility for permits and inspections.


I thought it would be worthwhile to bring these items to your attention before the agreement proceeds further for review and execution.


Best,

subject: Stonehaven Marketplace – Preliminary Glendale Sign Code Summary (05/29/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,



Below is a consolidated summary of the Glendale sign code provisions that appear most relevant to the Stonehaven Marketplace Comprehensive Sign Plan.


Property Information

*	APN: 102-11-010P
*	Zoning: PAD (Planned Area Development)
*	General Plan: Planned Commercial (PC)
*	Approximate Frontages:

	*	W Camelback Road: 995.9 LF
	*	N 91st Avenue: 890.4 LF

________________________________

Freestanding Monument Signs

Number Allowed

*	One (1) monument sign per 200 linear feet of street frontage.

Maximum Height

*	14 feet along Major Arterial Roads and Parkways.

Maximum Sign Area

*	110 square feet per sign for parcels over 20 acres located along Major Arterial Roads.

Preliminary Observation

*	Based on frontage calculations, up to three (3) monument signs could theoretically be supported along Camelback Road and up to three (3) along 91st Avenue.
*	However, actual sign placement must consider corner spacing, visibility triangles, driveways, landscape areas, and overall site design.
*	The currently proposed concept of two (2) monument signs per frontage appears to be a practical and defensible approach.

________________________________

Directional Signs

*	Directional signs are permitted.
*	Maximum area: 6 square feet.
*	Maximum height: 3 feet.
*	Intended to assist vehicular circulation and traffic flow.

________________________________

Building-Mounted Signs

Glendale does not distinguish between "Major Tenants" and "Minor Tenants."

Instead, allowable building sign area is based on:

*	Tenant frontage
*	Tenant square footage
*	Building sign standards contained in Section 35.4.311

General Commercial Uses

*	2 square feet of sign area per 1 linear foot of tenant frontage.
*	Minimum allowance: 50 square feet.

Maximum Total Building Sign Area

Tenant Size

Maximum Total Sign Area

Less than 20,000 SF

150 SF

20,000 SF – 40,000 SF

250 SF

Greater than 40,000 SF

450 SF

Multiple Building Elevations

*	Wall signs are permitted on each façade of a structure.
*	The code regulates total allowable sign area rather than assigning a specific allowance to each side of the building.

Example

*	Tenant with 40 LF frontage:

	*	40 LF × 2 SF/LF = 80 SF allowable sign area.

*	Tenant with 25 LF frontage:

	*	Minimum allowance of 50 SF would apply.

________________________________

Tenant Panels on Monument Signs

*	I did not locate a specific Glendale code limitation on the number of tenant panels.
*	Tenant panel quantity, layout, and hierarchy are typically established within the Comprehensive Sign Plan itself.

________________________________

Recommendation

The Glendale code provides the baseline allowances. The Comprehensive Sign Plan should establish:

*	Major Tenant standards
*	Minor Tenant standards
*	Pad building sign standards
*	Monument sign tenant panel standards
*	Directional sign standards
*	Overall design consistency throughout the development


This appears to be the same general approach used in other Glendale Comprehensive Sign Plans.


Best,

Hi Rocky,

Here are the direct answers to your questions:


Building Sign Area (Major vs. Minor Tenants)
    • Glendale's sign code does not establish separate square footage allowances for "major tenants" versus "minor tenants."
    • Building sign area is generally calculated based on each tenant's linear frontage and applicable building sign standards contained in Section 35.4.311.


Number of Signs Per Elevation
    • The code does not appear to limit a tenant to only one sign per elevation.
    • The focus is on the total allowable sign area rather than a specific number of wall signs.


Four-Sided Pad Buildings
    • Yes, pad buildings are generally allowed signage on multiple sides.
    • Elevations facing public streets, drive aisles, and prominent customer-facing areas are typically eligible for signage.
    • The allowable square footage is determined based on the qualifying frontage and applicable code provisions.


Recommendation
    • I recommend we follow the same approach used in the City's approved 303 & Bethany Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) example.
    • That CSP does not establish detailed major-tenant/minor-tenant wall sign standards. Instead, it states that all building-mounted signs will be reviewed and approved under the standard City of Glendale Sign Ordinance.
    • This keeps the CSP clean and allows future tenant signage to be reviewed under the City's current code requirements.


I'm attaching the 303 & Bethany CSP example for reference.  Let me know if able to be of any additional assistance.

subject: RE: U-Haul Sahuarita – Proposed Comprehensive Sign Plan Review (05/29/26)
body:
Hi Dylan,

 

Thank you for taking the time to review the package and provide the feedback.

 

This was exactly the type of preliminary input we were hoping to receive before preparing a formal CSP submittal, and I appreciate you identifying the sign area concerns early in the process.

 

We will revisit the proposed sign program and evaluate the elevations against the Town's allowable sign area requirements and CSP criteria. Based on your comments, it appears we will need to reduce portions of the proposed signage package and better align the application with the available CSP incentives.

 

We will also incorporate the additional application materials you referenced, including:

• Total proposed sign area by frontage, sign type, and overall project total
• Maximum allowable sign area by frontage, sign type, and overall project total, including calculation methodology
• Detailed explanation of any requested deviations
• Written justification supporting any proposed deviations

 

Thank you as well for clarifying the limitations of the CSP process and the practical application of the 20% increase provisions. That information is extremely helpful as we refine the proposal.

 

We will continue working with Orlanthia as we revise the package and prepare the next iteration for review.

 

Thank you again for your assistance and enjoy your vacation.

 

Best regards,

 

Steve Skye

Subject: Re: U-Haul Sahuarita – Proposed Comprehensive Sign Plan Review (05/28/26)

 

Steve,

 

I did a quick review of what you submitted. The amount of signage you are proposing would not be allowed even with an approved CSP. The CSP allows for up to a 20% increase in sign area with Planning & Zoning Commission approval. The South elevation is currently proposing over a 100% increase from the 225 sq. feet maximum allowed. There are other elevations that also exceed what would be allowed with a CSP. Based on the proposed signs your CSP application would most likely not qualify for all of the elements that contribute to the allowable 20% increase. I would recommend reviewing the 4 criteria that provide 5% increases.

I realize that this was not a complete submittal but also wanted to give you a heads up that your application materials need to provide items F, G and H from the required elements in the code, also listed below.

 

*     Total proposed sign area per frontage, per sign type, and overall for the project.

 

*     Maximum allowed sign area per frontage, per sign type, and overall for the project, and explanations of how the maximums were calculated.

 

*     If the applicant proposes a deviation from the standards set forth in this chapter, the following additional information shall be provided:

    

*         A detailed explanation of the deviations being proposed.

 

*         A written justification for the deviations.

 

 

If you have any questions, please contact Orlanthia as I will be on vacation for a few weeks.

 

Thanks,

Dylan

Estimates and services should be assumed to be consistent with standard industry service offerings for obtaining a permit. Special requests or requests above and beyond what is typical must be communicated.

				6. Project estimates are based on an expected level of effort, experience, and time across various internal functions using one standardized company rate. Specific billable rates and time per rate cannot be broken out.

				7. Project estimates do not include shipping, printing, additional copies, additional forms, shop reviews, or any other accessory services outside of the base deliverable unless specifically communicated.

				8. Estimated project timelines are typically based on the presumption that the proposed design concept is generally adequate and all necessary information is provided at the time of award. Inadequate design concepts (which may or may not be apparent until a certain level of analysis is performed) or incomplete information may require additional time to complete the service request and may require additional billable time should the scope need to materially change.

				9. Final service fees may vary with additions or changes that materially alter the work effort such as, but not limited to::

				a. Additional client or jurisdictional requirements

				b. Specific or atypical project requests or requirements

				c. Additional requests or information that materially alter the work effort

				e. Peer review or plan check comments

				f. Response Letters, forms, and other official correspondence

				g. Meetings and conferences not specifically requested by the engineer.

				10. The engineered design will match any provided shop-level or fabrication drawings as closely as possible where specific design information exists. Reverence Engineering will assume that provided specifications are purposeful and will not alter elements of the design unless code compliance, safety, or company standards dictate. Where specific information is not shown or otherwise provided, a reasonable engineered solution will be provided. 

				11. Official plan check comments other than those stemming directly from errors or omissions as they relate to the contracted scope of work are considered additional billable. 

				12. Reverence Engineering is not familiar with and does not research jurisdictional administrative requirements. Any administrative requirements affecting the base deliverable (such as formatting) must be communicated to Reverence Engineering. Additional fees may apply.

It is the responsibility of the client to provide all appropriate information for consideration in analysis and design development. Such assumptions may not accurately represent actual field conditions and additional engineering services may be required to address site conditions at a later date.

				14. It is the responsibility of the fabricator and/or installer to verify all field conditions before procurement of parts and materials and before fabrication.

				7. Project estimates do not include shipping, printing, additional copies, additional forms, shop reviews, or any other accessory services outside of the base deliverable unless specifically communicated.

subject: U-Haul Sahuarita – Permit Application Status Update (05/27/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,



I corresponded with the Town of Sahuarita concerning the status of the U-Haul permit application.


At this point, the Town is requiring the project to proceed through a formal Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) review process rather than continuing as a standard sign permit application.


The good news is that the existing artwork and exhibit package already substantially satisfies much of the CSP content requirements. The issue does not appear to be the design itself, but rather the formal administrative process the Town wants the project routed through.


The primary remaining items appear to be:
• Development Review / CSP application package
• CSP narrative / written justification
• Sign area calculations
• Identification and justification of any code deviations
• Owner authorization documentation


The current artwork package is likely already 70–80% of what will ultimately be needed for the CSP submission.


The recommended next step is to coordinate directly with Larry Myers to confirm the exact CSP submission requirements and checklist before assembling the final package for formal Development Review routing.


Please see the attached status summary for reference.


Best regards,

Thank you again for taking the time to meet with me regarding the proposed freeway pylon concepts for Chandler Fashion Center.


Attached are the revised artwork concepts incorporating the updates and direction discussed during our meeting for your review.


Based on our discussion, I explored several revised tenant panel configurations and overall proportions for the scale of a 75’ freeway pylon. During the meeting, you wanted us to explore smaller 5' x 20' tenant panels and that felt somewhat undersized relative to the overall scale and visual mass of the proposed freeway pylon, so we shrunk the girth of the sign without reducing it in height to make that size of a tenant panel look proportionately correct. subject: RE: CHANDLER FASHION
body:
Hi Andy and Monica,



Thank you again for taking the time to meet with me regarding the proposed freeway pylon concepts for Chandler Fashion Center.


Attached are the revised artwork concepts incorporating the updates and direction discussed during our meeting. I will also be sending a completed presentation package which will include additional nighttime renderings/examples for review.


Based on our discussion, I explored several revised tenant panel configurations and overall proportions for the display. During the meeting, it appeared that the 5' x 20' tenant panels felt somewhat undersized relative to the overall scale and visual mass of the proposed freeway pylons. In response, I developed additional options utilizing 6' x 25' tenant panels, which remain smaller than the original concept while, in my opinion, providing improved balance and visibility for signage of this scale.


The attached concepts are intended to provide comparative options for review and discussion as the project direction continues to evolve.


Please take a look through the revised concepts and let me know your thoughts, preferences, or any additional adjustments you would like us to explore.


Thank you again, and I look forward to your feedback.

700 N Dysart Rd
Goodyear, AZ 85338

*	Disconnect switch location
*	Confirmation the disconnect is within sight of the sign
*	Voltage / circuit identification
*	Branch circuit information
*	Disconnect accessibility
*	Dedicated circuit notation (if applicable)
*	Additional sign power routing detail

Hi Frank,



Thanks again for speaking with me this morning.



To “measure twice and cut once” and hopefully avoid another review cycle, if possible, I am providing the attached for reference:

*	The current County redlines / review markups
*	A sample Maricopa County submittal package showing additional code and NEC reference information previously required on other County sign permits


After reviewing the current County comments again, I do not specifically see the reviewer directly calling out:

*	Maricopa County adopted code references

subject: Easelife Spa – Sign Criteria & Branding Information (05/19/26)
body:
Hi Anthony,



Thank you again for taking the time to speak with me today regarding the proposed signage for your Easelife Spa suite at The Camp at Black Canyon.


As discussed, the center appears to have a unique and specialized sign program, so before we begin developing concepts or pricing, could you please reply with any available sign criteria / tenant signage requirements associated with the property? These are often included within the lease documents as an appendix or exhibit (commonly “Appendix A” or a signage criteria package).


This will allow us to review:

*	Permitted sign types
*	Size limitations
*	Colors / materials
*	Illumination requirements
*	Typography / design restrictions
*	Landlord approval requirements

Additionally, if you have any existing branding materials such as:

*	A business card
*	Logo files
*	Preferred type style / font
*	Existing artwork or inspiration images
	…please send those as well so we can begin evaluating a sign design that fits both your branding and the center requirements.


Once we review the criteria package, we can begin preparing recommendations and a quotation for the proposed signage.

Hi Mackenzie,



Thank you for the quick follow-up and clarification.


Regarding the address comment — the City of Goodyear typically wants the project location address shown directly on the plan set, generally within the title block or drawing identification area on each sheet. I believe that is what they are referring to rather than the artwork itself.


The project address should appear as:

700 N Dysart Rd
Goodyear, AZ 85338


Regarding the electrical comments, I agree the request is somewhat vague. I reviewed the drawing package and there are already electrical notes included within the plans. 


My assumption is the city is requesting additional clarification related to NEC Article 600 disconnect requirements, potentially including:

*	Disconnect switch location
*	Confirmation the disconnect is within sight of the sign
*	Voltage / circuit identification
*	Branch circuit information
*	Disconnect accessibility
*	Dedicated circuit notation (if applicable)
*	Additional sign power routing detail


They may also simply want the disconnect location shown more explicitly on the elevation or site-related view.


Thank you as well for coordinating the Owner Authorization document — once received, that should satisfy the remaining administrative requirement.


If helpful, we can also contact the city directly at 623-932-3004 for clarification prior to preparing the resubmittal package.  I would be happy to set up a conference call so we can address these items together.  Please let me know…

subject: RE: MWC Monument Sign Estimate (05/12/26)
body:
Hi Mireille,



Thank you for reviewing the estimate.


The “LED retrofit” portion refers to replacing the existing internal illumination components within the monument sign cabinet with all new LED lighting components. Based on the age of the existing sign, the current lighting system is likely older and may already have partial outages or may become unreliable soon.


The retrofit would include:
• Removal of the older illumination components
• Installation of new LED modules and power supplies
• New internal illumination for the updated sign faces
• Improved brightness, efficiency, and long-term reliability


The new LED components also include a 7-year manufacturer warranty, which helps provide long-term peace of mind and reduces the likelihood of future maintenance costs associated with aging lighting systems.


The sign faces themselves would still be replaced either way; the LED retrofit is simply the optional upgrade to renew the internal lighting system at the same time while the cabinet is already open and being serviced.


Please let us know if you feel the additional investment into the new illumination system is worthwhile for the project, or if you would prefer to proceed with only the new sign faces and cabinet refinishing.


We look forward to seeing the finalized artwork revision including the website and phone number.


Best regards,

body:
Hi Frank,



Please see the attached correction comments from the County regarding the Grease Monkey #1493 permit application.


The County is becoming increasingly strict concerning 2018 IBC Section 107.2 and is emphasizing that the permit drawings must reflect a “definite and complete design.”


The primary remaining concerns appear to be:
• Mounting hardware not fully specified for wall conditions
• Foundation details for the directional signs
• Corrosion protection at aluminum post/concrete connections
• Missing referenced engineering details
• General clarification that all structural / connection details must be fully defined on the permit set


The reviewer specifically noted that previous comments from prior reviews remain unresolved on Sheets 8, 9, 11, and 12.


If desired, I can also investigate coordinating a conference call with the reviewer to discuss the remaining comments directly and determine the best path toward approval.


Please review and let me know how you would like to proceed.

subject: Exalted Homecare – Sign Ordinance Review (05/12/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,



Attached is the completed Sign Ordinance Report for the Exalted Homecare property located at 3602 S Central Ave in Phoenix.


After reviewing the zoning maps and Phoenix Sign Ordinance requirements, the property appears zoned C-3 (General Commercial) and fronts South Central Avenue, which is classified as a high-volume arterial street. The site is not located within the formal Central Avenue Corridor district, so the stricter corridor sign provisions do not appear to apply.


The proposed existing pole sign configuration appears generally supportable under Section 705 / Table D-1 standards.


Key takeaways from the review:

*	Proposed sign height: approximately 14'
*	Proposed sign face area: approximately 32 SF
*	Allowed primary ground/pole sign height: 16'
*	Allowed primary ground/pole sign area: 110’


Based on the ordinance review, the proposed sign falls below both the standard height and allowable sign area limitations for a primary freestanding sign along a high-volume street.


The sign will still require:

*	Sign permit review
*	Structural / engineering review
*	Electrical review if illuminated
*	Field verification by the City of Phoenix


Overall, the ordinance review appears favorable for permitting the existing sign structure and proposed face size.

subject: Hayden Professional Center – Pre-Application Review Summary (05/12/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,



Attached is the pre-application review summary and CSP compliance notes for the Hayden Professional Center project following the discussion with the City of Scottsdale Planning staff.


Based on the review, the site does appear to allow freestanding signage opportunities; however, the existing CSP and MSP framework remain highly controlled, and an MSP/CSP amendment will likely still be required depending on the final sign concepts pursued. The city also identified several additional site planning, architectural, and residential adjacency considerations that will need to be addressed as we move forward.


Some of the primary items discussed included:

• Existing awnings are not currently approved
• Proposed signage is expected to be in the awning areas
• Illuminated individual letter signage appears acceptable on the street elevations.
• No illuminated signage facing residential areas
• CSP amendment anticipated for the proposed work
• Site triangle, setback, and PUE constraints will affect placement
• Additional Planning review should be expected


I also noted that the city appears focused on maintaining architectural consistency throughout the center, which will likely influence any proposed design direction.


Please review the attached summary when you have a chance. We should probably discuss potential design approaches and determine the most feasible path before advancing further into formal entitlement work.

body:
Hi Rocky,



Attached are the zoning and sign ordinance reports for the Cocina Madrigal project located at 4040 S 16th St in Phoenix.


The most important portion of the review relates to the City of Phoenix Table D-1 freestanding sign allowances for commercial properties located on high volume streets.



📐 Table D-1 – Freestanding Sign Allowances


Primary Freestanding Sign
• Maximum Height: 16 ft
• Up to 20 ft through Design Review
• Maximum Sign Area: 110 sq ft
• Up to 150 sq ft through Design Review


Secondary Freestanding Sign
• Maximum Height: 12 ft
• Up to 15 ft through Design Review
• Maximum Sign Area: 80 sq ft
• Up to 110 sq ft through Design Review


Source: City of Phoenix Zoning Ordinance Section 705 – Table D-1 Identification Signs.


📘 Additional Table D-1 Notes

• 16th Street is classified as a high volume street.
• One primary sign is generally permitted per 300 linear feet of frontage.
• One secondary sign is generally permitted per 150 linear feet of frontage.
• Design Review approval may allow increased height and sign area.
• Corner parcel provisions may provide alternate sign configurations.


⚠️ Key Restrictions

• No signs permitted within visibility triangles.
• No signs projecting into public right-of-way.
• No portable ground signs permitted.
• Animated signage prohibited without approval.
• Illumination must comply with Dark Sky requirements.


Please review and let me know if you would like us to evaluate any Design Review opportunities or alternate sign configurations based upon the existing site conditions and frontage.

Following our review of the revised Burger King #16449 construction drawings, we found that several of the items previously requested by the Pinal County planner are still not fully addressed within the current drawing package.

• Frontage measurements for each elevation
• Allowable sign area calculations
• Individual proposed sign area calculations by elevation
• Total combined proposed sign area
• A written explanation describing how frontage measurements were determined

For your consideration, please find below our General Service Understandings:

 

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

General Service Understandings  ← Updated January 2024: please familiarize yourself!

1. The base deliverable is a digital set of structural drawings (11x17) and an accompanying set of structural calculations (8.5x11) produced by Reverence Engineering unless communicated otherwise.

2. The base deliverable will be stamped and signed by an engineer appropriately licensed in the subject jurisdiction. Reverence Engineering does have partner engineers employed for specialty or small-volume jurisdictions; all work is performed and managed at Reverence Engineering, but the final stamp by the licensed engineer may read differently.

3. The base deliverable shall convey the structural intent and basis for design conformance. The base deliverable is not a fabrication or shop-level set of drawings and will likely not include shop-level specificity and components not part of the structural system.

4. All features under a project request will be provided in one package unless requested differently before commencing work or if already part of a pre-engineered program. Separating features into individual packages will incur an additional fee after work has commenced.

5. Project estimates (when issued) are typical and based on information available at the time the estimate is issued. Estimates and services should be assumed to be consistent with standard industry service offerings for obtaining a permit. Special requests or requests above and beyond what is typical must be communicated.

6. Project estimates are based on an expected level of effort, experience, and time across various internal functions using one standardized company rate. Specific billable rates and time per rate cannot be broken out.

7. Project estimates do not include shipping, printing, additional copies, additional forms, shop reviews, or any other accessory services outside of the base deliverable unless specifically communicated.

8. Estimated project timelines are typically based on the presumption that the proposed design concept is generally adequate and all necessary information is provided at the time of award. Inadequate design concepts (which may or may not be apparent until a certain level of analysis is performed) or incomplete information may require additional time to complete the service request and may require additional billable time should the scope need to materially change.

9. Final service fees may vary with additions or changes that materially alter the work effort such as, but not limited to::

a. Additional client or jurisdictional requirements

b. Specific or atypical project requests or requirements

c. Additional requests or information that materially alter the work effort

d. Requests or information that creates rework

e. Peer review or plan check comments

f. Response Letters, forms, and other official correspondence

g. Meetings and conferences not specifically requested by the engineer.

10. The engineered design will match any provided shop-level or fabrication drawings as closely as possible where specific design information exists. Reverence Engineering will assume that provided specifications are purposeful and will not alter elements of the design unless code compliance, safety, or company standards dictate. Where specific information is not shown or otherwise provided, a reasonable engineered solution will be provided. 

11. Official plan check comments other than those stemming directly from errors or omissions as they relate to the contracted scope of work are considered additional billable. 

12. Reverence Engineering is not familiar with and does not research jurisdictional administrative requirements. Any administrative requirements affecting the base deliverable (such as formatting) must be communicated to Reverence Engineering. Additional fees may apply. 

13. Reverence Engineering is not responsible for the accuracy of existing or field conditions. It is the responsibility of the client to provide all appropriate information for consideration in analysis and design development. Where information cannot be provided or verified, Reverence Engineering may make assumptions about the existing conditions for permitting purposes at the direction of the client. Such assumptions may not accurately represent actual field conditions and additional engineering services may be required to address site conditions at a later date.

14. It is the responsibility of the fabricator and/or installer to verify all field conditions before procurement of parts and materials and before fabrication. 

15. Reverence Engineering does not “rubber stamp” client-produced documents. Should a jurisdiction require that client-produced drawings (ie, a brand book or art deck) be stamped for permitting purposes, Reverence Engineering must have already produced an independent base deliverable for each feature shown. Client-produced drawings must then be reviewed and reconciled to remove possible discrepancies. An additional fee will apply. Reverence Engineering will not modify documents produced by others; all modifications must be performed by the owner of such documentation.

16. Once a project deliverable is provided for review, the client shall be afforded 21 calendar days (3 weeks) to review the project documents. Before the end of the review period, the client may elect to suspend the project for up to 60 days; the client will be assessed a 1-hour reactivation fee at the then-current company standard rate to resume services. Should there be no meaningful progress by the end of the review period and/or the suspension period, the project will be automatically closed and invoiced for services performed; reactivation of the project at a later date will be subject to a reactivation fee plus any services to be performed to include compiling a final approved set of documents. Projects with an outstanding 100% review set will be invoiced at 100% of the estimated fee plus any additional services performed less any services specifically estimated and not performed.

17. This estimate is valid for 30 calendar days. We will make efforts to follow up via email approximately 3 and 10 days after the estimate is issued.

subject: Burger King #16449 – Pinal County Sign Criteria / Permit Requirements (05/06/26)
body:
Hi Team,



I was able to speak with Valentyn from the Planning Department at Pinal County regarding the Burger King #16449 project and reviewed the applicable sign criteria associated with the 2006 CSP.



Based on our discussion, it appears the County is no longer requiring a separate Comprehensive Sign Plan review for this parcel.


Below are the primary items needed for the permit package and sign calculations:

*	The 2006 CSP still applies to the site
*	Sign allowance is based on building frontage
*	Allowance calculation:

	*	1 linear foot of frontage = 2 square feet of sign area

*	Frontage dimensions are needed for each building elevation
*	Each elevation will require:

	*	Frontage measurements
	*	Individual sign area calculations

*	Total sign area calculations will also be needed for all elevations combined
*	The County is requesting a detailed explanation showing:

	*	How frontage was measured
	*	How the sign area calculations were derived

Additional Notes:

*	The project has been set up in the portal
*	Follow-up communication is needed with Sabine Johnson (call/email)
*	Requirements were discussed directly with Valentyn, Planner for Pinal County


Please let me know how we are to best proceed with updating the proposed project submittals.


Best,

Steve Skye

body:
Hi Derrick,

 

Thank you again — we appreciate the opportunity to help on this project.

 

You are correct regarding the window graphics terminology. After reviewing the original construction package, the correct description should be opaque first-surface vinyl logo graphics installed onto the existing glazed/frosted surface. The frosting itself was an existing condition and was not installed as part of our scope. I will revise that wording in the report accordingly.

 

Regarding the wall condition beneath the acrylic hallway signs, the peeled paint/drywall condition was existing prior to our installation. Our team noted the wall surface condition during install, particularly in the hallway locations shown in the photos.

 

Thank you for catching the wording clarification before client closeout. Overall, I think the project turned out very well and we appreciate all the coordination from your team to help get this completed quickly.

 

Please let me know if there is anything further needed from our side.

 

Thank you,

subject: Jas Diesel – Permit Approved / Next Step (05/01/26)
body:
Hi Team,



I wanted to provide an update on the Jas Diesel project and outline our path forward.



The permit has now been approved by the City of Phoenix. The project has also been revised as shown in the updated artwork (attached).


As discussed, we will need to procure the fuel price changer units from the manufacturer (Optec), their cutsheet is attached for reference. This differs from the originally planned display and will require integration once received.


To keep the project moving and meet the customer’s timeline, we will proceed with installation of the sign structure and cabinets first, with the price changers to be installed later once delivered. The cabinets are complete, and the pole is already set in the footing onsite.


The customer has emphasized the need to begin advertising fuel pricing as soon as possible and is requesting installation by 05/23. In the interim, we may utilize the electronic message center in a static format or provide a temporary/manual pricing solution until the permanent price changers are installed.


Before scheduling the official City footing inspection, we need to complete an internal pre-inspection of the footing to confirm readiness.



Next Steps:
• Perform internal footing pre-inspection
• Schedule City of Phoenix footing inspection
• Proceed with cabinet installation
• Order Optec price changers (8–10 week lead time) 
• Coordinate temporary pricing solution if required


Please review and advise if there are any concerns before we move forward.

Good afternoon, Christina,

Thank you for speaking with me today.


I reached out to the City of Mesa today and confirmed that Michele Large is the assigned reviewer on this project. I left her a voicemail and have included her here so we can coordinate directly on this clarification.


We are looking for guidance on the illumination requirement noted in the review comments, specifically:

• For a remote letterset wall sign (no background panel), is the building façade considered the “background”?
• Does the requirement that “only the sign copy be illuminated” limit illumination strictly to the text (“Clayton Homes”)?
• Would the chevron/logo element be permitted to be illuminated, or should it remain non-illuminated (or halo-lit only)?


We reviewed Section 11-43-2 of the Mesa sign code, which appears to address internally illuminated signs with opaque backgrounds. Since this is a remote letterset, we want to ensure we are interpreting the requirement correctly before proceeding with any revisions.


For now, we recommend holding on any design changes until we receive confirmation from Ms. Large to avoid unnecessary rework.


Please let us know the preferred direction when you have a moment, and we’ll proceed accordingly.

subject: RE: Burger King #16449 – Permit Status Update (04/29/26)
body:
Hi Joshua,



Thank you for following up.


Based on feedback from Pinal County, a Comprehensive Sign Review (CSR) is required for this project. This is a separate application from the sign permit and is necessary due to the scope of the proposed signage.


We have begun reviewing the CSR requirements and are currently evaluating the scope of work needed to prepare and submit the application. Once that review is complete, we will provide an estimate for the additional effort required to process and obtain CSR approval.


Please note that the CSR will need to be processed under a separate order, as it is outside the original permit scope. In addition, the County application fee of $1,187.00 must be paid upfront to initiate the review process.


For reference, our CSR scope will include:
• Preparation of a justification narrative describing the signage and design intent
• Compilation of a complete sign package (all proposed signage, sizes, and details)
• Site plan and building elevations showing sign locations
• Documentation of any existing signage on the property
• Coordination with property ownership for authorization
• Submission through the County’s planning portal for review


Once the CSR is submitted and approved, the sign permit application can proceed through the normal review process.


I’ll keep you updated as we finalize scope and next steps. Please let me know if you have any questions in the meantime.


Thanks,

 

Steve Skye

Hi Jacob,

Thank you for your review and for the additional insight — we appreciate the clarification.


We have updated the submittal in the portal and are including the revised artwork here for reference .

In response to your request, we have also attached the manufacturer schematics and product information for the proposed price changer units. These documents illustrate that the price panels are purpose-built numeric LED displays intended for fuel pricing applications, rather than full-color electronic message displays.


Specifically, the Optec Digit-PC units:
• Are configured for fixed numeric character output (fuel pricing formats)
• Do not support full-color graphics, messaging, or video content
• Utilize segmented LED digit architecture rather than pixel-based display systems
• Are designed for pricing display use only, with limited functionality beyond numeric values


Additionally, the attached shop drawings show the physical construction and configuration of the price changer cabinets, which differ from the full-color display unit proposed above .


Our intent with this revision is to clearly separate the pricing component from the electronic message display portion of the sign.


Please let us know if the current submittal satisfies the requirements, or if there is any additional information you would like us to provide.
