Jacob,

Thank you for your review and detailed feedback.


We would like to provide clarification regarding the EMD square footage calculation noted in the corrections.


Per the approved Use Permit stipulations, the maximum electronic message display (EMD) area is limited to 40 square feet . Our understanding and intent is that this requirement applies specifically to the programmable message display portion of the sign.


The current design includes:

*	40 square feet of electronic message display (EMD) used for changeable messaging 
*	20 square feet of fuel price displays, which are static price changers 


The fuel price components:

*	Are not used for messaging or advertising 
*	Do not function as an electronic message center 
*	Are regulated separately, as fuel pricing is required to be continuously and accurately displayed for operational compliance 


Because of this distinction, the fuel price displays should not be considered part of the EMD area calculation. The EMD portion of the sign remains compliant with the 40 square foot limitation as outlined in the Use Permit.


Additionally, we note that the prior approval did not include stipulations restricting the configuration in this manner , further supporting the interpretation that the EMD limitation applies specifically to the message display portion.


We would appreciate your confirmation on this interpretation so we may proceed accordingly without unnecessary redesign.


Thank you,

subject: Castle Megastore – CSP Amendment Status Update (04/24/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,



I wanted to provide a status update on the Castle Megastore (Hayden Plaza) sign permit application.


I spoke with Joe Cruz (Field Inspector), who confirmed that due to the change in design from the existing sign, the project will require a Minor Amendment to the Hayden Plaza North Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP). While the scope is a replacement, the revised design triggers the amendment requirement under the City’s review standards.


Based on that direction, we have moved forward with preparing and submitting the required project narrative to the City for review. This narrative outlines the removal of the existing sign and installation of the new double-faced pylon sign, including updated structure and footing.


We have also sent the narrative directly to Otis Harris (Sign Inspector) for confirmation that the submittal meets their expectations.


At this stage:
• Minor Amendment path has been confirmed by the city
• Project narrative has been submitted
• Awaiting feedback from Otis / Sign Department
• Estimated review timeframe is approximately 2–3 weeks


Next steps will be to respond to any City comments (if issued) and proceed toward approval so we can move into permitting.


I’ll keep you posted as soon as we hear back.


Let me know if you have any questions in the meantime.

I wanted to provide a quick update on the Hayden Professional Center project.


We have successfully submitted the request for a Pre-Application Meeting with the City of Scottsdale to evaluate the feasibility of updating the existing Comprehensive Sign Program (CSP) to allow for freestanding monument signage.


The City has acknowledged receipt of the application and assigned the following reference number:



PA-0470-2026


At this stage, we are awaiting initial review comments and scheduling from the Planning Department. All updates will be issued through the Scottsdale SPUR portal, and we will monitor for any feedback or required next steps.


This meeting will be an important step in confirming whether the city will support a CSP amendment for monument signage and what criteria they will expect us to meet.


I’ll keep you posted as soon as we receive any updates or scheduling information.

Scottsdale encourages its customers to be aware of an email phishing scam in which the sender impersonates city staff and requests payment using fraudulent invoices.

body:
Hi Jacob,



Thank you for your review and for the additional insight — we appreciate the clarification.


We have updated the submittal in the portal and are including the revised artwork here for reference .

In response to your request, we have also attached the manufacturer schematics and product information for the proposed price changer units. These documents illustrate that the price panels are purpose-built numeric LED displays intended for fuel pricing applications, rather than full-color electronic message displays.


Specifically, the Optec Digit-PC units:
• Are configured for fixed numeric character output (fuel pricing formats)
• Do not support full-color graphics, messaging, or video content
• Utilize segmented LED digit architecture rather than pixel-based display systems
• Are designed for pricing display use only, with limited functionality beyond numeric values


Additionally, the attached shop drawings show the physical construction and configuration of the price changer cabinets, which differ from the full-color display unit proposed above .


Our intent with this revision is to clearly separate the pricing component from the electronic message display portion of the sign.


Please let us know if the current submittal satisfies the requirements, or if there is any additional information you would like us to provide.


Thank you again for your time and guidance.


Best regards,

Hi Jacob,

Thank you for your review and for raising this concern.


We understand the question regarding the display’s ability to present content beyond fuel pricing. The attached Fuel Price Display Narrative outlines the intended use and operational framework of the fuel price panels.


In practice, when operated in a static setting, the display functions the same as a fuel price changer, presenting fixed pricing rather than variable messaging.


In the same manner that the City’s Use Permit establishes how the display must be operated—including automatic shutoff at 10:00 PM, display timing requirements, and brightness limits not to exceed 300 nits—the static fuel price display is achieved through system configuration and operation.


We have also included Cirrus documentation demonstrating that the display system can maintain a fixed image, control brightness, and implement scheduled operation to meet these requirements.


The fuel price panels operate within this same compliance-based framework and are used to display fuel pricing only.


Please let me know if you would like any additional detail or to review the system configuration further.

Jacob,

Thank you for your review and detailed feedback.


We would like to provide clarification regarding the EMD square footage calculation noted in the corrections.


Per the approved Use Permit stipulations, the maximum electronic message display (EMD) area is limited to 40 square feet . Our understanding and intent is that this requirement applies specifically to the programmable message display portion of the sign.


The current design includes:

*	40 square feet of electronic message display (EMD) used for changeable messaging 
*	20 square feet of fuel price displays, which are static price changers 


The fuel price components:

*	Are not used for messaging or advertising 
*	Do not function as an electronic message center 
*	Are regulated separately, as fuel pricing is required to be continuously and accurately displayed for operational compliance 


Because of this distinction, the fuel price displays should not be considered part of the EMD area calculation. The EMD portion of the sign remains compliant with the 40 square foot limitation as outlined in the Use Permit.


Additionally, we note that the prior approval did not include stipulations restricting the configuration in this manner , further supporting the interpretation that the EMD limitation applies specifically to the message display portion.


We would appreciate your confirmation on this interpretation so we may proceed accordingly without unnecessary redesign.


Thank you,

subject: Stotz Equipment – Survey Scope & Site Plan Requirements (Permit Coordination) (04/23/26)
body:
Hi Chris,



Following review of the County’s correction comments, we need to clarify the required deliverable for permit resubmittal.


At this stage, the County is requiring a stamped and engineer scaled site plan that clearly documents right-of-way and easement constraints for the property.


To proceed, please incorporate the following into a formal, permit-ready site plan:



• Sealed, engineer/surveyor-stamped site plan
• Property boundaries clearly defined
• Future / reserved right-of-way (Miller Road) shown and labeled
• All recorded easements shown (type and width, consistent with Schedule B/title report)
• Required setbacks clearly indicated (including approx. 25’ from property line per MCDOT)
• Dimensions from property lines to ROW and easement limits
• Confirmation (graphically and/or by note) that structures cannot be placed within ROW or easement areas


The intent is for your plan to clearly define the site constraints. The final sign location will be determined by Pattison ID and the client based on visibility, electrical access, and site considerations.


The permit is currently on hold due to right-of-way and easement verification requirements, so this deliverable is critical for resubmittal.


This plan will be submitted directly to the County and should be formatted and stamped accordingly.


I’ve provided the correction notes and plans for your reference.


Please let us know if you need anything further from our side to complete this.


Thank you,

Good afternoon, Christina,



Thank you for speaking with me today.


I reached out to the City of Mesa today and confirmed that Michele Large is the assigned reviewer on this project. I left her a voicemail and have included her here so we can coordinate directly on this clarification.


We are looking for guidance on the illumination requirement noted in the review comments, specifically:

• For a remote letterset wall sign (no background panel), is the building façade considered the “background”?
• Does the requirement that “only the sign copy be illuminated” limit illumination strictly to the text (“Clayton Homes”)?
• Would the chevron/logo element be permitted to be illuminated, or should it remain non-illuminated (or halo-lit only)?


We reviewed Section 11-43-2 of the Mesa sign code, which appears to address internally illuminated signs with opaque backgrounds. Since this is a remote letterset, we want to ensure we are interpreting the requirement correctly before proceeding with any revisions.


For now, we recommend holding on any design changes until we receive confirmation from Ms. Large to avoid unnecessary rework.


Please let us know the preferred direction when you have a moment, and we’ll proceed accordingly.

subject: Burger King #16449 – CSR Requirement & Next Steps (04/20/26)
body:
Hi Scott,

 

I wanted to provide you with an update on the Burger King #16449 permit (SIGN26-00024) for your customer.

• Elevation frontage calculations

body:
Hi Rocky,



I reviewed the zoning and sign ordinance for the Bible Holiness Church property (see attached reports).


The site is zoned RM-2 (residential), so signage is permitted but fairly limited in scale. Because it’s a religious institution, it qualifies for the non-residential allowances within that zone.



• Freestanding signs: Up to 2 per street frontage, max 32 sq. ft. each, and up to 8’ in height

subject: Castle Megastore – Artwork Revisions, Design Review & Code/CSP Summary (04/17/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,



I wanted to follow up with a consolidated review of the Castle Megastore sign based on the field inspection, artwork, and applicable City/CSP requirements.


First, the artwork needs to be corrected. The current set references reusing the existing pole and footing, however based on updated understanding this is a new structure (new pipe and footing). The drawings should be revised to:

• Remove all references to “existing pole” and “existing footing”
• Reflect a new engineered pole and foundation
• Include appropriate ASA/engineered footing detail for submittal


From a zoning/code standpoint:

• The site is zoned C-2 (Intermediate Commercial)
• The sign falls under commercial ground sign standards (Section 705)
• Proposed sign area is 64 sq. ft., which is well within the allowable limits
• Proposed height appears to be approximately 20’-0”, which exceeds the 16’ allowance by right and will require Design Review approval


We should plan on submitting this with a Design Review request to justify the height, which is common and typically approvable for this type of corridor.


On the CSP side, we reviewed the Hayden Plaza North Comprehensive Sign Plan. The document is dated (originally 1999 with minor amendments for prior tenants such as Home Depot and T-Mobile) and does not provide clear or current enforceable standards for height or sign area. It functions more as a design guideline than a controlling document.


Our position should be:
• The proposed sign is consistent with the overall intent and character of the CSP
• The design complies with current City of Phoenix sign code requirements
• Therefore, the application should be evaluated primarily under Section 705


Next steps:
• Revise artwork to reflect new structure and footing
• Prepare for Design Review submittal (height justification)
• Confirm footing/engineering detail is included in permit package


Let me know if you want me to coordinate the revisions or handle the Design Review narrative.


Best,

subject: NextCare – Sign Evaluation & Recommended Approach (04/16/26)
body:
Hi Anna,

I wanted to follow up regarding the NextCare Urgent Care location in Apache Junction and share our findings from the recent site evaluation (see attached report) .


While the original scope was to perform an LED retrofit and address the current outages, our field review identified a broader issue. In addition to the electrical failures (including multiple letter outages and failed transformers), the sign is also experiencing significant material degradation. The acrylic faces are cracked, the vinyl is deteriorating, and overall components are showing signs of age-related wear.


Because of this, proceeding with a retrofit alone would not provide a reliable long-term solution. Retrofitting LED into compromised letter faces would likely result in inconsistent illumination and continued failures, leading to additional service calls.


Based on these conditions, we recommend a combined approach:
• Remove the existing neon system
• Install a new LED illumination system
• Replace all letter faces with new acrylic and vinyl


This will restore proper illumination, improve overall durability, and bring the sign up to current standards.


Please look at the attached report and let me know if you’d like to review this together or discuss next steps. We’re happy to assist in developing a revised scope or proposal based on this recommendation.


Warm regards,

*	Estimated LED dies (RGB 3-in-1): 3 × 4,608 = 13,824 LED dies per module

Physical Dimensions

After reviewing the portal (see attached screenshot ), it appears we currently have a mix of application statuses that need to be cleaned up and brought to closure. These generally fall into three categories:

• Ready for Issuance / Fees Due – Applications that are approved but pending payment
• Issued / Pending Final – Permits that now require inspection scheduling and close-out
• Inactive / No Longer Needed – Applications that may need to be formally withdrawn or cancelled


Now, these are sitting in various stages without a coordinated push to completion, which is what prompted the City’s follow-up.


Additionally, this is not isolated to Avondale — we are seeing similar situations across other jurisdictions where permits are either awaiting fees, inspections, or finalization. This would be a good opportunity to treat this as a focused cleanup effort across the board to:

• Clear out outstanding fees
• Schedule and complete required inspections
• Close out or cancel any inactive permits
• Bring all records to a finalized state


This is not urgent in the immediate sense, but it does require dedicated attention to prevent ongoing follow-ups from jurisdictions and to keep our records current and clean.


Let me know when you’d like to prioritize this, and I can begin organizing a structured list and action plan to work through everything efficiently.

subject: Avondale Sign Permit Applications – Status Cleanup Needed (04/15/26)
body:
Hi Wendy,



We have recently received three separate emails from the City of Avondale (Linda Hearing, Sign Department) regarding outstanding sign permit applications that require attention.


After reviewing the portal (see attached screenshot ), it appears we currently have a mix of application statuses that need to be cleaned up and brought to closure. These generally fall into three categories:



• Ready for Issuance / Fees Due – Applications that are approved but pending payment
• Issued / Pending Final – Permits that now require inspection scheduling and close-out
• Inactive / No Longer Needed – Applications that may need to be formally withdrawn or cancelled


Now, these are sitting in various stages without a coordinated push to completion, which is what prompted the City’s follow-up.


Additionally, this is not isolated to Avondale — we are seeing similar situations across other jurisdictions where permits are either awaiting fees, inspections, or finalization. This would be a good opportunity to treat this as a focused cleanup effort across the board to:

• Clear out outstanding fees
• Schedule and complete required inspections
• Close out or cancel any inactive permits
• Bring all records to a finalized state


This is not urgent in the immediate sense, but it does require dedicated attention to prevent ongoing follow-ups from jurisdictions and to keep our records current and clean.


Let me know when you’d like to prioritize this, and I can begin organizing a structured list and action plan to work through everything efficiently.


Best regards,



Steve Skye

Hi Derrick,



Thank you for taking a close look at this — I appreciate you flagging it.


I believe the confusion is coming from the deposit invoice versus the estimate breakdown, so let me clarify:

subject: Chandler Review Corrections – Chick-fil-A #2567 (04/13/26)
body:
Hi Scott,



I wanted to bring to your attention the review comments issued by the City of Chandler Sign Department for the Chick-fil-A #2567 project (SGN26-0083).


The City has completed their initial review and provided corrections that will need to be addressed prior to permit approval.


At a high level:

• The site plan currently reflects a proposed layout that has not yet been approved by Planning. Because of this, the reviewer cannot approve the plan as submitted.
• The reviewer has marked certain ground signs to be omitted for now. They are requesting that we revise the plan set and resubmit without those signs so that the wall signs and remaining signage can be approved.
• Once Planning approves the overall site layout, a subsequent submittal will be required for the omitted ground signs.


Additionally:

• All drive-thru directional signs must be reduced to a maximum height of 3'-0" (36").
• Future resubmittals must clearly show all directional sign locations and confirm compliance with this height requirement.


In summary, we can proceed by revising the current plan set to remove the flagged signs and move forward with approval of the wall signage, while the ground signs will follow after Planning finalizes the site plan.


I’ve attached the full correction set for your review. Let me know how you’d like to proceed, and we can begin coordinating the revisions.


Best regards,

subject: DiMaggio’s Sign Concept Direction (Horizontal Sign Option)
body:
Hi Frank,



I spoke with our design team regarding the horizontal option, and we do think that direction has potential. A horizontal layout would allow us to create a strong display incorporating the logo and neon elements and overall would read better than a projecting-type sign.


Attached is a photo of the southwest elevation (taken during the original sign installation). Based on this, we think it may be worth considering placing the display in that location.


Given the building conditions and available wall space, a wall-mounted sign would likely be the stronger solution here. This elevation provides a clean, visible surface that would allow us to:

• Improve visibility from the primary approach
• Simplify structural and permitting requirements
• Create a more cohesive look with the building façade
• Avoid limitations tied to the existing bracket system


If you’re open to it, we can put together a few wall sign concepts that carry that classic DiMaggio’s identity—incorporating the vintage/neon feel we discussed—just applied in a way that better fits the architecture.


Let me know your thoughts and we’ll move quickly in whichever direction you’d like to pursue.


Warm regards,



Steve Skye

subject: Hayden Professional Center – CSP Amendment / Pre-Application Meeting Request (04/08/26)
body:
Hi Alex,



I hope you’re doing well.


I wanted to follow up on the voicemail I left earlier today regarding the Hayden Professional Center. We would like to proceed with scheduling a Pre-Application Meeting to evaluate a potential amendment to the existing Master Sign Program.


We’ve reviewed the Master Sign Programs information provided on the City’s website and understand the process to generally be as follows:



• Initiate a Pre-Application Meeting with Planning
• Provide a narrative outlining the scope and justification for the request
• Submit conceptual materials, including a site plan and preliminary design intent
• Following pre-application feedback, proceed with a formal CSP amendment submittal for administrative review


Our intent is to explore the feasibility of introducing a freestanding (monument-style) signs, as this is not currently permitted under the existing CSP. We are in the process of preparing the necessary conceptual materials and justification to support this request.


Would you mind reviewing the above understanding and confirming that we are aligned with the City’s expectations? Additionally, please let us know the best way to initiate and schedule the Pre-Application Meeting, including any specific submittal requirements or forms we should be aware of.


We appreciate your guidance and look forward to working through this process with you.


Best regards,

 

Steve Skye

subject: Jas Diesel – Fuel Price Display Revision (04/08/26)
body:
Hi Jeb,



I wanted to update you on the Jas Diesel project regarding the fuel price display portion of the sign.


We have been working with the city to support the use of the Cirrus selected display system as a static fuel price display. This was outlined in our Fuel Price Display Narrative, explaining that the panels would be operated strictly for fuel pricing despite the system having message center capabilities.


However, the city is requiring that the fuel price portion utilize technology limited to traditional price-changing features. They are not accepting the use-based argument and are instead classifying the display based on its underlying technology.


To keep the project moving forward, we will revise the design to incorporate a traditional price changer. We have attached the Optic price changer cutsheet for reference , which will require us to rework the artwork and layout of the sign.


With this change, there should be no remaining barriers to obtaining permit approval for the sign.


This revision will impact the overall aesthetic, as we will no longer be able to maintain a consistent display appearance between the message center and the pricing panels, but it aligns with the City’s requirements and clears the path to approval.


We will begin updating the artwork accordingly and will share the revised layout for your review shortly.


Please let me know if you have any questions in the meantime.


Best regards,



Steve Skye

subject: Hayden Professional Center – Signage Constraints & Next Steps (04/07/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,



I wanted to follow up with an update on the Hayden Professional Center project now that we have received and reviewed the existing Comprehensive Sign Program (CSP).


Based on the attached analysis, the current CSP does not permit traditional freestanding signage (monument or pylon). Signage on this site is limited to building-mounted signs and a very specific type of “freestanding wall signage,” which must be mounted to existing architectural walls — not new structures.


In short, the current program does not support a new freestanding sign under its existing framework.


That said, I have reached out to Alex Bohlin with the City of Scottsdale and left her a message to discuss the project further. The goal is to get guidance directly from Planning and determine whether a freestanding sign could be supported through an alternative path, such as a CSP amendment or Design Review Board process.


At this point, we are not blocked — but we will likely need City support to move beyond the current limitations of the CSP.


I will follow up with you as soon as I connect with Alex and can outline the most viable path forward.


Please let me know if you have any questions in the meantime.


Best regards,

Jacob,

Thank you for your review and detailed feedback.


We would like to provide clarification regarding the EMD square footage calculation noted in the corrections.


Per the approved Use Permit stipulations, the maximum electronic message display (EMD) area is limited to 40 square feet . Our understanding and intent is that this requirement applies specifically to the programmable message display portion of the sign.


The current design includes:

*	40 square feet of electronic message display (EMD) used for changeable messaging 
*	20 square feet of fuel price displays, which are static price changers 


The fuel price components:

*	Are not used for messaging or advertising 
*	Do not function as an electronic message center 
*	Are regulated separately, as fuel pricing is required to be continuously and accurately displayed for operational compliance 


Because of this distinction, the fuel price displays should not be considered part of the EMD area calculation. The EMD portion of the sign remains compliant with the 40 square foot limitation as outlined in the Use Permit.


Additionally, we note that the prior approval did not include stipulations restricting the configuration in this manner , further supporting the interpretation that the EMD limitation applies specifically to the message display portion.


We would appreciate your confirmation on this interpretation so we may proceed accordingly without unnecessary redesign.


Thank you,

subject: Jas Diesel – Fuel Price Display Issue (Use Permit Review) (04/02/26)
body:
Hi Wendy,



I wanted to bring you up to speed on an issue we’ve encountered with the Jas Diesel project regarding the fuel price display portion of the sign.


We have been working with the city to clarify that the price display will be operated as a static fuel price changer, even though the selected display platform has electronic message center capabilities. This position is outlined in the attached Fuel Price Display Narrative, which explains that the display will be configured and operated strictly for fuel pricing in accordance with Arizona regulations and the Use Permit requirements.


This approach has been accepted in the past; however, it appears that the interpretation of the Use Permit stipulations has changed. The inspector is now taking the position that the classification is based on the technology itself rather than how it is used.


Despite our efforts to explain that the system will remain static and operate within the same compliance-based framework as the approved EMC, I have not been able to convince the inspector otherwise. They are requiring that the fuel price portion utilize technology that is limited to price-changing features only, like traditional fuel pricers.


Cirrus does not manufacture this type of limited-function price changer, and as a result, complying with this requirement would impact the overall sign aesthetic and eliminate the consistent appearance between the message display and pricing panels.


At this point, we may need to determine whether to revise the design to meet this interpretation or escalate the issue for further clarification from Planning.


Please let me know how you would like to proceed.


Best regards,



Steve Skye

subject: Bodybar – Gilbert Window Graphics Review (04/02/26)
body:
Hi Scott,



I’ve reviewed the proposed Bodybar window graphics against the Town of Gilbert sign code.


Gilbert does allow window signage; however, it is limited to a maximum of 25% window coverage, which includes vinyl, painted graphics, and any applied window films.


Based on the current design, the blackout graphics appear to exceed this allowable coverage, so as proposed, it would not meet code compliance.


We would either need to revise the layout to fall within the 25% limitation or pursue approval through a Comprehensive Sign Plan (if applicable to the site).


Let me know how you’d like to proceed.

Best,



Steve Skye

Hi Jacob,



Thank you for your review and for raising this concern.


We understand the question regarding the display’s ability to present content beyond fuel pricing. The attached Fuel Price Display Narrative outlines the intended use and operational framework of the fuel price panels.


In practice, when operated in a static setting, the display functions the same as a fuel price changer, presenting fixed pricing rather than variable messaging.


In the same manner that the City’s Use Permit establishes how the display must be operated—including automatic shutoff at 10:00 PM, display timing requirements, and brightness limits not to exceed 300 nits—the static fuel price display is achieved through system configuration and operation.


We have also included Cirrus documentation demonstrating that the display system can maintain a fixed image, control brightness, and implement scheduled operation to meet these requirements.


The fuel price panels operate within this same compliance-based framework and are used to display fuel pricing only.


Please let me know if you would like any additional detail or to review the system configuration further.


Best regards,

Jacob,

Thank you for your review and detailed feedback.


We would like to provide clarification regarding the EMD square footage calculation noted in the corrections.


Per the approved Use Permit stipulations, the maximum electronic message display (EMD) area is limited to 40 square feet . Our understanding and intent is that this requirement applies specifically to the programmable message display portion of the sign.


The current design includes:

*	40 square feet of electronic message display (EMD) used for changeable messaging 
*	20 square feet of fuel price displays, which are static price changers 


The fuel price components:

*	Are not used for messaging or advertising 
*	Do not function as an electronic message center 
*	Are regulated separately, as fuel pricing is required to be continuously and accurately displayed for operational compliance 


Because of this distinction, the fuel price displays should not be considered part of the EMD area calculation. The EMD portion of the sign remains compliant with the 40 square foot limitation as outlined in the Use Permit.


Additionally, we note that the prior approval did not include stipulations restricting the configuration in this manner , further supporting the interpretation that the EMD limitation applies specifically to the message display portion.


We would appreciate your confirmation on this interpretation so we may proceed accordingly without unnecessary redesign.


Thank you,

Hi Derek,



Good to hear from you — hope all is well on your end.


Yes, we can point you in the right direction on the color. I’ve attached the original artwork along with the 3M color reference used on the sign for your reference .


The burgundy used on the sign corresponds to 3M Translucent Film – 3630-49 (Burgundy). That would be the closest standard reference to match.

For paint, I’d recommend taking that reference (or a printed sample from the attachment) to your paint supplier and asking for a custom color match. 

Most suppliers (Sherwin-Williams, Dunn-Edwards, etc.) can scan and match this very closely in an exterior-grade finish.

If helpful, you can ask for:
• A satin or semi-gloss exterior enamel (depending on your preference)
• Color match to 3M 3630-49 Burgundy

subject: Jas Diesel – Fuel Display Clarification & Brightness Requirement (03/31/26)
body:
Hi Rebekah,



Thank you again for taking the time to speak with me earlier today — I appreciate it.


I wanted to follow up regarding the Jas Diesel project. We are currently working through plan review comments with the city, and one of the key items relates to the fuel price display portion of the sign.


The reviewer’s concern is tied to the drawings identifying both the message display and fuel price panels similarly, and specifically noted:

“The ability to display something other than the price of fuel is what I am concerned with.”


To address this, we have prepared a narrative (attached) clarifying that the fuel price panels are used strictly for fuel pricing in accordance with Arizona regulatory requirements, and that the system is operated in a manner consistent with static price displays.


To help support this with the city, we are looking to provide a bit more clarity from the manufacturer side. Would you be able to assist with the following:

• A brief description or statement confirming that the display system can be operated to present fixed (non-changing) content, such as fuel pricing
• Any guidance or documentation on how this type of use is typically configured or managed within the system


Additionally, the city has requested the following:

• Electrical certification confirming that the display does not exceed 300 nits brightness


If Cirrus has a standard specification sheet, certification, or statement addressing brightness levels (or the ability to limit brightness), that would be very helpful for our submittal.


The goal here is simply to provide clarity on how the system is used in practice so the city can feel comfortable with the distinction and move the permit forward.


Thanks again for your help on this — I appreciate your support.


Best regards,



Steve Skye

	Jacob,

	Thank you for your review and detailed feedback.

	
	We would like to provide clarification regarding the EMD square footage calculation noted in the corrections.

	
	Per the approved Use Permit stipulations, the maximum electronic message display (EMD) area is limited to 40 square feet . Our understanding and intent is that this requirement applies specifically to the programmable message display portion of the sign.

	
	The current design includes:

	*	40 square feet of electronic message display (EMD) used for changeable messaging 
	*	20 square feet of fuel price displays, which are static price changers 

	
	The fuel price components:

	*	Are not used for messaging or advertising 
	*	Do not function as an electronic message center 
	*	Are regulated separately, as fuel pricing is required to be continuously and accurately displayed for operational compliance 

	
	Because of this distinction, the fuel price displays should not be considered part of the EMD area calculation. The EMD portion of the sign remains compliant with the 40 square foot limitation as outlined in the Use Permit.

	
	Additionally, we note that the prior approval did not include stipulations restricting the configuration in this manner , further supporting the interpretation that the EMD limitation applies specifically to the message display portion.

	
	We would appreciate your confirmation on this interpretation so we may proceed accordingly without unnecessary redesign.

	
	Thank you,

	Jacob,

	Thank you for your review and detailed feedback.

	
	We would like to provide clarification regarding the EMD square footage calculation noted in the corrections.

	
	Per the approved Use Permit stipulations, the maximum electronic message display (EMD) area is limited to 40 square feet . Our understanding and intent is that this requirement applies specifically to the programmable message display portion of the sign.

	
	The current design includes:

	*	40 square feet of electronic message display (EMD) used for changeable messaging 
	*	20 square feet of fuel price displays, which are static price changers 

	
	The fuel price components:

	*	Are not used for messaging or advertising 
	*	Do not function as an electronic message center 
	*	Are regulated separately, as fuel pricing is required to be continuously and accurately displayed for operational compliance 

	
	Because of this distinction, the fuel price displays should not be considered part of the EMD area calculation. The EMD portion of the sign remains compliant with the 40 square foot limitation as outlined in the Use Permit.

	
	Additionally, we note that the prior approval did not include stipulations restricting the configuration in this manner , further supporting the interpretation that the EMD limitation applies specifically to the message display portion.

	
	We would appreciate your confirmation on this interpretation so we may proceed accordingly without unnecessary redesign.

	
	Thank you,

Jacob,

Thank you for your review and detailed feedback.


We would like to provide clarification regarding the EMD square footage calculation noted in the corrections.


Per the approved Use Permit stipulations, the maximum electronic message display (EMD) area is limited to 40 square feet . Our understanding and intent is that this requirement applies specifically to the programmable message display portion of the sign.


The current design includes:

*	40 square feet of electronic message display (EMD) used for changeable messaging 
*	20 square feet of fuel price displays, which are static price changers 


The fuel price components:

*	Are not used for messaging or advertising 
*	Do not function as an electronic message center 
*	Are regulated separately, as fuel pricing is required to be continuously and accurately displayed for operational compliance 


Because of this distinction, the fuel price displays should not be considered part of the EMD area calculation. The EMD portion of the sign remains compliant with the 40 square foot limitation as outlined in the Use Permit.


Additionally, we note that the prior approval did not include stipulations restricting the configuration in this manner , further supporting the interpretation that the EMD limitation applies specifically to the message display portion.


We would appreciate your confirmation on this interpretation so we may proceed accordingly without unnecessary redesign.

Jacob,

Thank you for your review and detailed feedback.


We would like to provide clarification regarding the EMD square footage calculation noted in the corrections.


Per the approved Use Permit stipulations, the maximum electronic message display (EMD) area is limited to 40 square feet . Our understanding and intent is that this requirement applies specifically to the programmable message display portion of the sign.


The current design includes:

*	40 square feet of electronic message display (EMD) used for changeable messaging 
*	20 square feet of fuel price displays, which are static price changers 


The fuel price components:

*	Are not used for messaging or advertising 
*	Do not function as an electronic message center 
*	Are regulated separately, as fuel pricing is required to be continuously and accurately displayed for operational compliance 


Because of this distinction, the fuel price displays should not be considered part of the EMD area calculation. The EMD portion of the sign remains compliant with the 40 square foot limitation as outlined in the Use Permit.


Additionally, we note that the prior approval did not include stipulations restricting the configuration in this manner , further supporting the interpretation that the EMD limitation applies specifically to the message display portion.


We would appreciate your confirmation on this interpretation so we may proceed accordingly without unnecessary redesign.


Thank you,

subject: Jas Diesel – Permit Status Update (03/30/26)
body:
Hi Jeb,

Monday Happiness!



I wanted to provide you with an update regarding the permit status with the City of Phoenix.


We have now heard back from the city. The Use Permit approval is currently subject to the standard 15-day appeal period, which will conclude on April 3rd.



In the meantime, the City has provided additional direction on what is needed to move the sign permit forward once the appeal period has cleared. The primary items include:

*	Updating the drawings to comply with the Use Permit stipulations (EMD area and brightness limits)
*	Providing certified electrical details confirming brightness does not exceed 300 nits
*	Addressing prior comments related to design review (including narrative and applicable fee)
*	Resolving the public utility easement issue (either relocation or utility signoffs)
*	Confirming no conflict with approved landscaping or obtaining City approval if adjustments are needed


We are currently reviewing and discussing these requirements internally so we can determine the best path forward and compile everything needed for resubmittal.


Our goal is to move through these items as efficiently as possible, and we hope to have everything addressed quickly following the appeal period.


I’ll keep you updated as we make progress. Please let me know if you have any questions in the meantime.


Best regards,

subject: RE: Jas Diesel – Sign Permit Follow-Up (LPSG 251389) (03/27/26)
body:
Jacob,



Thank you for your review and detailed feedback.


We would like to provide clarification regarding the EMD square footage calculation noted in the corrections.


Per the approved Use Permit stipulations, the maximum electronic message display (EMD) area is limited to 40 square feet . Our understanding and intent is that this requirement applies specifically to the programmable message display portion of the sign.


The current design includes:

*	40 square feet of electronic message display (EMD) used for changeable messaging 
*	20 square feet of fuel price displays, which are static price changers 


The fuel price components:

*	Are not used for messaging or advertising 
*	Do not function as an electronic message center 
*	Are regulated separately, as fuel pricing is required to be continuously and accurately displayed for operational compliance 


Because of this distinction, the fuel price displays should not be considered part of the EMD area calculation. The EMD portion of the sign remains compliant with the 40 square foot limitation as outlined in the Use Permit.


Additionally, we note that the prior approval did not include stipulations restricting the configuration in this manner , further supporting the interpretation that the EMD limitation applies specifically to the message display portion.


We would appreciate your confirmation on this interpretation so we may proceed accordingly without unnecessary redesign.


Thank you,

 

Steve Skye

subject: Uni K Wax – Paradise Valley Sign Update (03/27/26)
body:
Hi Sarah,

Welcome to Friday!



Good question — and glad the city was able to clarify that.


Since the original sign permit has already been issued, that approval is tied specifically to the design and scope that was submitted and approved under that permit.


In this case:

*	We would not be able to proceed with a set of channel letters on the tenant panel under the existing permit, as it would fall outside the approved scope.
*	A new permit application will be required to reflect the channel letter design and sizing.
*	The city will typically assess a new permit fee, as this will be treated as a new review based on the revised scope.


The good news is that since the city has already confirmed the allowable signage parameters, the review should be more straightforward — we’ll just need to formalize it through a new submittal.

subject: Castle Megastore – Update & Next Steps (LPSG 260223) (03/26/26)

Hi Rocky,



Following up on my last update—there has now been movement on the City’s review.


The reviewer has classified the proposed ground sign as an additional sign under the Hayden Plaza CSP, which would typically require a Major Amendment / Use Permit. We’ve clarified that the scope is a replacement of an existing sign, not a new addition.


I also connected with the field inspector, who indicated the existing sign may not have been previously permitted, which is likely influencing the City’s position.


At this point, we’ve submitted a Public Records Request to obtain the Hayden Plaza CSP so we can confirm the original sign criteria and determine the correct path forward (see below).

Raceway Visibility
The Town is requiring that the raceway not be visible. It will need to be concealed or integrated into the façade so that it is not exposed.


Sign Area Reduction (CSP Requirement)
Under the Chandler Heights Village Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP), the allowable sign area is based on the leased frontage. subject: NEC Hayden & McDowell – Monument Sign Feasibility Summary (03-17-26)
body:
Hi Rocky,



I’ve completed a preliminary review of the Scottsdale sign code and evaluated the property at the northeast corner of Hayden Rd & McDowell Rd. I’ve attached a Sign Ordinance & Entitlement Report for your reference.  Here is a summary of what we found:



1. Monument Sign Feasibility
Freestanding monument signage is not permitted by right under the current PNC zoning. Any new monument signs would require approval through Scottsdale’s Design Review Board (DRB) process.

2. Size Limitations (Code-Based)
Under standard code allowances:

*         Maximum height: approximately 5 feet

*         Maximum area: 24 sq. ft. per face
These are typically limited to entry identification signage, not larger commercial monument signs.

3. Site Considerations

*         No Master Sign Program (MSP) is on file for the property

*         No existing monument signage appears to have been previously entitled

*         Scottsdale applies a strict design review standard, which suggests signage was either not pursued or limited during original development

4. Recommended Approach
If ownership proceeds with the acquisition, the most viable path would be:

*         Pursuing a directory-style monument sign

*         Preparing a Design Review Board submittal demonstrating:

o    Traffic visibility needs

o    Site circulation benefit

o    Architectural compatibility with the center

While signage is not guaranteed, entitlement may be achievable with a well-structured submittal.


Once you’ve had a chance to review, I can move forward with concept designs and preliminary pricing based on a DRB-driven approach.


Let me know how you’d like to proceed.


Best,

 

Steve Skye

subject: Jas Diesel – Use Permit Hearing This Thursday
body:
Hi Jeb,

Happy Monday !



I wanted to let you know that I will be attending the Use Permit hearing for the sign this Thursday (03/19) at 1:30 PM.

*	Town of Queen Creek Corrections Report
*	Harvest Station Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP)
*	Current First Watch sign drawings and elevations


In summary, the Town is requiring revisions in two key areas:

1.	Wall Sign / Raceway Design
	The proposed wall signs do not currently meet the CSP requirement for architecturally integrated raceways. The CSP requires individual channel letters integrated into a designed signage wireway or sign band that is complementary to the building architecture, rather than a standard exposed raceway. The sign details and elevations will need to be revised accordingly.
2.	Sign Area Calculations
	The submittal must clearly document building frontage dimensions and provide sign area calculations per the CSP (1.5 SF per linear foot, max 250 SF per building). These calculations need to be shown directly on the plans.

• Prepare the amendment drawings and documentation

• Coordinate the City of Surprise permit or clearance process after DRC approval

Please submit a Building Permit inspection so that you can move forward with your project and avoid having to fill out a permit extension form. 

 

Once the inspection has been processed, the new expiration date will be set for 180 days from the processing date, and you will be able to schedule more inspections.

 

Attached is the inspection request directions. 

 

Please review this attachment and schedule your inspections to prevent any delay.

Happy Friday !



Following up on our review of the property and applicable City of Phoenix sign standards, we have prepared a concept rendering for the proposed freestanding sign at your location at 4325 S. 34th St. Please see the attached artwork for your review. 


The high-profile sign concept was already part of the original design ideas, so we left that option included for reference. In addition, we developed a monument-style sign concept that may provide a strong presence for the property.

Hi Taryn,

I wanted to follow up regarding PMT26-01022 – Sherwin-Williams (1202 University Dr.) and your correction comment under §11-43-2B1.a.i or ii.

We recently spoke with a Planner of the Day, who reviewed the proposed sign plans and recognized that the signs are pan-channel letters mounted on a backer panel, not cabinet signs. 

This configuration itself appears to meet the intent of §11-43-2B1.a.i (individual letters), but we understand that the current plan set did not clearly communicate that distinction.


To clarify the construction method, we are providing the attached channel letter installation cut sheet, which demonstrates how the pan-channel letters are mounted and wired, including attachment and structural details. This should eliminate any ambiguity regarding the sign type and confirm that it is not a standard rectangular cabinet.


Please let us know if this documentation will satisfy the review requirement, or if you would like us to incorporate additional clarification directly into the plan set for resubmittal.

Also, we need assistance in uploading them via the portal.


Thank you for your time and review.


Best regards,

Subject: RE: Crumbl–Peoria - Allowed Sign Area Confirmation (01/16/26) 

 

Hi Sarah,

Thanks for the question — this is a good one.


I reviewed both the City of Phoenix Sign Ordinance and the Metro Towne Center Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) to confirm the allowable sign area for this location.


Although the tenant frontage is approximately 25 feet, the City of Phoenix code provides a minimum wall sign allowance of 50 square feet for commercial tenants. This comes directly from Phoenix Sign Ordinance Table D-1, which states:

“Wall Signs – Commercial: 1 square foot of sign area per 1 linear foot of building frontage (minimum 50 square feet).”


Because the ordinance establishes a 50 sq ft minimum, the normal frontage-based calculation (25 LF = 25 sq ft) does not apply here.


The Metro Towne Center CSP does not reduce this allowance — it regulates sign type and design standards, not overall area. The CSP permits aluminum pan channel letters for shop tenants and defers to the city ordinance for allowable square footage.  Based on both the Phoenix Sign Ordinance and the CSP:

• The maximum allowable area for the Crumbl primary wall sign is 50 square feet
• This allowance applies even with a 25’ tenant frontage
• Flush-mounted channel letters up to 50 sq ft total are permitted


You can therefore size the letters and logo however needed, provided the overall sign copy fits within a 50 sq ft envelope.


Please let us know if able to be of any additional assistance.

Sarah,


Yes — your understanding is correct.


Under the Metro Towne Center CSP, the key requirement is that the sign copy be aluminum pan channel letters and not a cabinet-style sign box. 

The CSP does not prohibit raceways or backer panels — it regulates the sign type, not whether the letters are mounted directly to the wall, to a mesh raceway, or to a solid raceway.


Tropical Smoothie is a good example of this. Their sign uses individual channel letters mounted to a solid raceway, which is allowed under the CSP, just as the mesh-style raceways used by Supercuts, Pizza Patrón, and Dickey’s are allowed. Crumbl can follow either approach.


So, for Crumbl:

*	The letters must be individual aluminum pan channel letters
*	They may be mounted to a painted mesh or solid raceway
*	The raceway should be painted to match the wall or approved background color
*	A beige background will be acceptable, subject to City approval, just as it is for Tropical Smoothie


As long as the drawings clearly show channel letters on a painted raceway (not a cabinet), the design will be CSP-compliant and should satisfy the City’s correction without requiring a Minor Amendment.

• Each sign requires its own dedicated 120V, 20-amp circuit.

Great question.


Yes — our installation includes making the final electrical connection to the signs. However, there are a couple of important requirements for illuminated channel letters:



• A junction box (J-box) must be located within approximately 6 feet of each sign location.
• Each sign requires a dedicated 120V, 20-amp breaker.


If those circuits are already in place at the building, we can complete the final connection as part of our install.


If power still needs to be run to the sign locations, that portion would need to be performed by a licensed electrician prior to our installation (we are not licensed for this). We can coordinate timing with your electrician to ensure everything is ready when the signs are delivered.

Reason for Notification

Notification Type: Bore Standby        Date: 02/27/2026

You have indicated on the Locate Request(s) that you intend to use Boring in your work area. To ensure the integrity of our system, Southwest Gas is requesting you call us prior to exposing our facilities. Southwest Gas requires a representative to be present to verify our facilities prior to boring across or parallel within 5-feet of Southwest Gas facilities. This is to confirm that you have in fact exposed our line and confirm the line depth to assure a safe bore operation by positive identification of our facilities. Call to schedule a standby a minimum of two hours prior to work identified above.

Notify an SWG representative when boring parallel to any Southwest Gas facilities within 5-feet of the bore. This applies to vertical boring as well.

1.	Notify an SWG representative when boring across any Southwest Gas facilities.
2.	Pothole any gas facilities within 24-inches of the proposed bore path.
3.	Hand digging is required within 24-inches of the gas facility markings, and all gas facilities must be identified, protected, and exposed during any boring operations.
4.	Before the excavation, schedule a Bore Standby with a SWG representative to be present to verify the buried facilities and monitor the boring activities.

Please contact your local SWG field office to schedule a Bore Standby with a Southwest Gas representative a

minimum of 2 hours prior.

 602-484-5086

 For more information regarding safe digging practices, please visit swgas.com

Locate Requester will notify its employees and any of their subcontractors of these requirements.

If you have any questions or need any assistance, please notify Southwest Gas immediately.

Southwest Gas Corporation Business Hours (Mon-Fri between 600 a.m. & 2:30 p.m.) After Hours Emergency: 877-860-6020

EXCAVATOR PRECAUTIONARY GUIDELINES

 

This information is to assist excavators in the proper identification of gas facilities, and precautions to be taken when working around gas facilities.  The information provided here is not to be considered all-inclusive. All excavators digging within the vicinity of gas pipelines must protect the pipelines in accordance with the applicable One-Call law. The following are guidelines that will assist you in protecting the public, you, and the gas facilities.

If any gas pipelines are damaged, federal law requires that you call Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Additionally, if the damage results in the escape of gas, you must call the Emergency Number 911.  Note: Damage includes damage to steel pipeline coatings, gouges in plastic pipe, damaged tracer wire, dents or scrapes in steel pipe, etc.

Gas pipeline markers are used to alert the public that gas pipelines are buried in the general area. These markers may or may not be placed directly over the gas facility. When performing an excavation within 10’ of a “High Pressure” marked facility, please contact SWG to arrange for stand by personnel to be present.

 

PLASTIC PIPELINES:  Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) pipe is one type of plastic pipe used in the SWG gas distribution system.  PVC may be faint yellow, gray or white in color and range in size from ½" to 2" in diameter.  PVC is not as flexible as the polyethylene (PE) pipe that SWG installs today. The integrity of PVC can be compromised if scratched or subjected to external loads and/or stresses.  PE is another type of plastic pipe used in SWG’s system.  PE may be found in various colors and range in size from ½" to 8" in diameter.  Although PE is a more flexible material, its integrity can be compromised if scratched or nicked.  Many plastic gas pipelines are installed with a tracer wire in order to locate the facility.  If a tracer wire is or has been severed or damaged, call SWG.  We will repair the damaged wire at no charge.

 

STEEL PIPELINES: Steel gas pipelines, used in both SWG gas distribution and high-pressure transmission systems, range in size from ½" to 24" in diameter and are also susceptible to damage.  Dents and gouges in the steel will affect the integrity of the pipe, so precautionary measures must be taken during excavation.  Steel pipelines are protected with an approved coating material that helps prevent deterioration of the pipe and can be found in various colors.  If during excavation the coating is torn or damaged, contact SWG immediately to facilitate the repairs at no charge.  Call us before disturbing any mastic coating on active or abandoned steel pipe.  The coating is likely to contain regulated asbestos fibers that can be harmful to your employees.

 

Typically, most gas pipes have specific identification markings on them or on the coating.  Care should be taken to support and protect all gas pipelines, as required by law, when exposed or crossed during excavation activities.  Additionally, care must be taken while exposing existing facilities as they may or may not have padding and shading surrounding them as outlined below.  If any gas pipeline is damaged, call SWG immediately to facilitate the proper pipeline repairs.  When excavations have been completed, gas pipelines must be properly padded, shaded, and backfilled per SWG standards, as shown in the drawing below.  SWG specifications for padding and shading material call for it to be able to sift through a 3/8" screen and be smooth and relatively rock free.  Excavations must be compacted to meet the requirements of local authorities.  During backfill activities it is very important to compact the soil beneath the gas pipe to properly support it. Also, it is important to avoid mechanically compacting the soil directly over the gas pipe to eliminate any unnecessary external stresses.  Steps must be taken during this process to protect the gas pipeline from excessive external loadings.  If other utilities or substructures are to be installed in the same excavation as a gas pipeline, the proper clearances shown in the drawing must be maintained.

If at any time during excavation activities you smell gas, call SWG and 911.

*	DO NOT attempt to control or stop the flow of natural gas, or make repairs.

*	DO NOT turn on, turn off, or attempt to move or operate equipment near the line break or point of leakage.

*	DO NOT enter the area where the natural gas is escaping.

*	DO NOT allow others to enter the area.

*	DO NOT leave the scene of the incident until assistance has arrived.

*	DO secure the area and prevent others from entering.

*	DO eliminate sources of ignition, such as sparks or flames, near the gaseous atmosphere.

For more information on the types of gas pipe used by SWG, positive identification of gas facilities, or if you have any questions, please contact the SWG office nearest you. Additional information on natural gas safety is included in our Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) located at www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .

Please forward to the appropriate excavator.



Esta información tiene como objetivo ayudar a los excavadores a identificar adecuadamente las instalaciones de gas y a conocer las precauciones que deben tener cuando trabajan cerca de ellas. La información aquí provista no es exhaustiva. Todos los excavadores que trabajen en cercanías de gasoductos deben protegerlos de acuerdo con la ley vigente sobre excavaciones. Las siguientes son pautas que lo ayudarán a proteger al público, a usted mismo y a las instalaciones de gas.

Si el gasoducto está dañado, la ley federal exige que llame a Southwest Gas Corporation (SWG). Además, si el daño causa un escape de gas, debe llamar al número para emergencias 911. Nota: Los daños pueden ser daños en el recubrimiento de las tuberías de acero, aberturas en las tuberías plásticas, daños en el alambre de rastreo, mellas o raspaduras en las tuberías de acero, etc.

 

Se usan señales para advertir al público de que hay gasoductos enterrados en el área. Estas señales pueden ponerse directamente sobre la instalación de gas o no. Cuando se lleva a cabo una excavación dentro de los 10’ de una instalación señalizada como “High Pressure” (de alta presión), comuníquese con SWG para que envíen personal de respaldo.

TUBERÍAS PLÁSTICAS Las tuberías de policloruro de vinilo (PVC) son un tipo de tubería plástica que SWG usa en el sistema de distribución. Las tuberías de PVC pueden ser de color amarillo claro, gris o blanco, y su tamaño puede ir desde ½” hasta 2” de diámetro. Las tuberías de PVC no son tan flexibles como las de polietileno (PE) que SWG instala hoy. El PVC puede arruinarse si se raya o se somete a pesos o tensiones extremos. Las tuberías de PE son otro tipo de tuberías plásticas que SWG usa en su sistema. Las tuberías de PE pueden ser de varios colores, y su tamaño va desde ½” hasta 8” de diámetro. Aunque el PE es un material más flexible, puede arruinarse si se raya o corta. Muchos gasoductos de plástico se instalan con un alambre de rastreo para ubicar la instalación. Si el alambre de rastreo se corta o daña, llame a SWG. Lo repararemos sin cargo.

 

TUBERÍAS DE ACERO Las tuberías de gas de acero, usadas por SWG tanto para la distribución de gas como para los sistemas de transmisión a alta presión, varían en tamaño desde 1/2" hasta 24" de diámetro y también son susceptibles a los daños. Las mellas y aberturas en el acero pueden afectar la integridad de la tubería. Por eso, deben tomarse medidas de precaución durante la excavación. Las tuberías de acero se protegen con un material de recubrimiento aprobado que ayuda a prevenir su deterioro y puede ser de varios colores. Si durante la excavación el recubrimiento se desprende o daña, comuníquese con SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones sin cargo. Llámenos antes de quitar cualquier recubrimiento de masilla de una tubería de acero activa o abandonada. Es posible que el recubrimiento contenga fibras de amianto reglamentario que pueden ser dañinas para sus empleados.

 

En general, las tuberías de gas tienen marcas de identificación específicas sobre ellas o sobre el recubrimiento. Debe tenerse precaución y sostener y proteger todos los gasoductos, según lo requiera la ley, cuando se expongan o crucen durante la excavación. Además, debe tenerse cuidado al exponer instalaciones existentes, ya que pueden o no, tener relleno a su alrededor, como se detalla más abajo. Si un gasoducto está dañado, llame a SWG de inmediato para facilitar las reparaciones necesarias. Cuando finalicen las excavaciones, los gasoductos deben ser rellenados según las normas de SWG, como se muestra en el dibujo más abajo. Las especificaciones de SWG para el material de relleno indican que este debe poder pasar a través de un tamiz de 3/8”, ser suave y estar relativamente libre de escombros.  Las excavaciones deben ser compactadas para cumplir con los requisitos de las autoridades locales. Durante el rellenado, es muy importante compactar el suelo bajo el gasoducto, a fin de sujetarlo apropiadamente. También es importante evitar compactar mecánicamente el suelo que está sobre el gasoducto para eliminar tensiones externas innecesarias. Deben tomarse medidas durante este proceso para proteger el gasoducto de cargas externas excesivas. Si se deben instalar otros servicios o subestructuras en la misma excavación del gasoducto, deben respetarse las distancias que se muestran en el dibujo.

Si en cualquier momento durante la excavación percibe olor a gas, llame a SWG y al 911.

*	NO intente controlar ni parar el flujo de gas natural ni de hacer reparaciones.

*	NO encienda, apague ni intente mover u operar equipos cerca del punto donde se rompió la línea o se produjo el escape.

*	NO entre en un área donde haya un escape de gas natural.

*	NO permita que otras personas entren en dicha área.

*	NO deje el lugar del incidente hasta que llegue la ayuda.

*	DESPEJE el área y evite que otras personas entren en ella.

*	ELIMINE las fuentes de combustión, como chispas o llamas, cerca de la atmósfera gaseosa.

Si desea más información sobre los tipos de tuberías de gas usados por SWG o sobre cómo identificar instalaciones de gas, o si tiene preguntas, llame a la oficina de SWG más cercana. En nuestra hoja de datos de seguridad de material (MSDS), puede encontrar más información sobre la seguridad con el gas natural. Esta se encuentra en www.swgas.com/emergencysafety <http://www.swgas.com/emergencysafety> .

 



Favor de hacer llegar al excavador correspondiente.

subject: First Watch #54530 – Gilbert Corrections Summary (02/27/26)
body:
Hi Scott,



We received correction comments from the Town of Gilbert on the First Watch #54530 sign permit application along with the applicable Crossroads Towne Center CSP requirements (see attached).  Below is a summary of what the reviewer is asking for:



• Elevation / Sign Band Information
They are requesting the length of each building elevation and the dimensions of the sign band area so they can verify the allowable sign area and confirm the 75% coverage limit required by the CSP.

• ASA / Frontage Calculation
The reviewer noted the allowable sign area must be calculated based on the storefront frontage per the CSP criteria and documented on the plans.

• Raceway Detail
The canopy letter detail shows an exposed raceway, and the CSP requires all electrical components to be concealed. They want that detail revised accordingly.


That’s the full scope of the comments — nothing unusual or outside typical CSP compliance documentation. Once the drawings are updated to reflect these items, we can proceed with the resubmittal.


Let me know if you’d like me to coordinate the revision package.


Thanks,

subject: Facility Preparation Complete – Property Owner Visit (02/25/26)
body:
Hi Wendy,



I wanted to let you know that we have completed the preparation for the upcoming property owner visit.


The ceiling tiles and lenses have been replaced, the office has been fully cleaned and organized, and the entry has been refreshed to present well upon arrival. The parking lot and walkways have been power washed, and the improvement is significant. The asphalt and concrete now appear much more uniform, and the overall curb appeal is noticeably stronger.


Attached are the latest photos reflecting the completed work, both interior and exterior. The facility presents as clean, orderly, and well maintained.


One item that remains is the interior lighting. The mismatched color temperatures and a few aging tubes are still noticeable. Given the timeline, we could not address that prior to the visit, but it is something we should plan to review afterward to achieve consistent lighting throughout.


We are looking forward to a positive visit.

Hi Sarah,



We received the first review comments from the City of Scottsdale for:



Uni K Wax
8776 E Shea Blvd #105
Plan Check #: 6180-25-2



I’ve attached the Correction Reports and Resubmittal Checklist for your reference. The primary issues noted by the City are as follows:



1. Sign Area Calculation / Code Analysis
The reviewer indicated that the code analysis is inaccurate. Because the sign is located less than 200 feet from the nearest right-of-way, the allowable sign area per elevation is 1 square foot per 1 linear foot of tenant frontage, or 12 square feet total, whichever is greater.

They are requiring verification of the tenant suite frontage dimension and revision of the sign area accordingly. Based on their markup, the currently proposed sign exceeds what is allowed under this calculation.

2. Additional Dimensions Required
The city is requesting:

?         Height, width, and length of all letters and logos

?         Horizontal and vertical spacing

?         Clarification of colors and materials

?         A sign section and installation detail

3. Suite Frontage & Floor Plan Documentation
They are requiring:

?         The length of the business suite frontage

?         A floor plan depicting the suite location

?         A site plan or aerial outlining the suite and sign location


The reviewer is Jason Katz, and this was Review Cycle 1 dated 02/23/2026.


At this stage, the most important item is confirming the tenant frontage dimension so we can determine the correct maximum allowable sign area and revise the layout if necessary.


Please review and let me know how you would like to proceed. I’m happy to go through the comments together and help coordinate the revisions for resubmittal.

Hi Taryn,

I wanted to follow up regarding PMT26-01022 – Sherwin-Williams (1202 University Dr.) and your correction comment under §11-43-2B1.a.i or ii.

We recently spoke with a Planner of the Day, who reviewed the proposed sign plans and recognized that the signs are pan-channel letters mounted on a backer panel, not cabinet signs. 

This configuration itself appears to meet the intent of §11-43-2B1.a.i (individual letters), but we understand that the current plan set did not clearly communicate that distinction.


To clarify the construction method, we are providing the attached channel letter installation cut sheet, which demonstrates how the pan-channel letters are mounted and wired, including attachment and structural details. This should eliminate any ambiguity regarding the sign type and confirm that it is not a standard rectangular cabinet.


Please let us know if this documentation will satisfy the review requirement, or if you would like us to incorporate additional clarification directly into the plan set for resubmittal.

Also, we need assistance in uploading them via the portal.


Thank you for your time and review.


Best regards,

subject: RE: Stotz Equipment – Sign Location / Permit Resolution (02/18/26)
body:
Hi Casey,



Thank you for the additional information — that’s very helpful.


If the sign is currently right at 25’ from the Miller Road property line, and there is the ability to shift it back a few additional feet, if necessary, that could be a viable resolution. However, since the County’s concern relates specifically to the future ROW line, we will need formal documentation to confirm compliance.


The most practical next step would be to perform a Boundary / Spot Survey to:

*	Verify the exact property line location
*	Dimension the sign pole to that property line
*	Confirm whether the sign is fully outside the future ROW
*	Identify any easements that may affect placement


This would provide a stamped exhibit we can submit to the County to demonstrate compliance and potentially avoid pursuing a ROW permit or relocating power.


Please let us know if you would like to move forward with this survey route to formally verify the setback and address the County’s requirements.


Once we have that documentation, we can confidently determine whether the existing location (or a minor adjustment) resolves the issue.


Best regards,

 

Steve Skye

Hi Jeremiah,

 

Thank you — I appreciate that. A tour would be helpful once we have a clearer direction.

 

Gilbert’s sign code can be rather restrictive, particularly if the property is zoned residential or Business Park. For example, in residential districts, high-mounted wall signage is generally not permitted unless it falls within a defined architectural sign band and meets specific dimensional criteria. Illumination can also be limited depending on adjacency. Because of this, we may have very limited options — possibly none — depending on the zoning designation.

 

Before proceeding with a site visit, survey, or proposal development, I’d like to confirm the zoning through the parcel number and have a preliminary discussion with the city to make sure we clearly understand what is permitted.

and the referenced code section:

What the City Is Requiring

Mesa is reviewing this as an attached permanent sign, and it must comply with §11-43-2B1.a.i or ii. That means the sign must be either:

Option 1 – Individual Letters

Pan channel (or similar durable) letters

No visible attachment devices

No standard rectangular cabinet

OR

Option 2 – Architecturally Designed Cabinet

Cabinet must be irregular and freeform in shape

Not a standard box-style cabinet

Mounting hardware cannot be visible

________________________________

What This Likely Means for This Submittal

The current design appears to be a rectangular aluminum cabinet, which does not meet Mesa’s design standards for attached signs.

Mesa is essentially asking that the sign either:

Be revised to individual channel letters, or

Be redesigned as an architecturally integrated, non-rectangular cabinet, or

Pursue a Comprehensive Sign Plan (CSP) if the standard cannot be met.


If helpful, I would be happy to hop on a conference call with Taryn Martinez (480-644-5459) to clarify exactly what they are looking for and confirm the most efficient path forward. A brief discussion can often prevent an unnecessary resubmittal cycle and provide clear direction.

subject: Burros & Fries – Gilbert Wall Sign Allowance / Frontage Clarification (02/17/26)
body:
Hi Rocky,



I wanted to provide a quick update on the Burros & Fries project in Gilbert.


Based on Table 5.6.11.E.2 (Wall Signs: 1-Story Building), the wall sign allowance is calculated off the length of the longest tenant elevation (or the elevation with the primary entrance) multiplied by:

*	1.0 if the building is < 75 ft from the ROW, or
*	1.5 if the building is > 75 ft from the ROW.


We understand the building appears to be greater than 75 feet from the ROW, so the 1.5 multiplier should apply.


However, before finalizing our calculations, there are three items we want to formally confirm with the Town:

1.	That the building is officially classified as > 75 ft from the ROW for purposes of applying the 1.5 multiplier.
2.	Whether the site qualifies under the Double Frontage provision (allowing cumulative sign allowance across two or more elevations).
3.	Whether the property is considered a corner lot for sign ordinance purposes, as that affects how frontage and cumulative allowance are interpreted.


I’ve left a message for Rohjn (Planner of the Day) to clarify these points so we can ensure our allowable area calculations align with the Town’s interpretation.


I’ll follow up as soon as I hear back so we can proceed confidently.


Best regards,

Hi Michelle,



Absolutely — here’s a simplified breakdown of what Mesa is asking for based on the correction notice 

and the referenced code section:



What the City Is Requiring

Mesa is reviewing this as an attached permanent sign, and it must comply with §11-43-2B1.a.i or ii. That means the sign must be either:

Option 1 – Individual Letters

*         Pan channel (or similar durable) letters

*         No visible attachment devices

*         Not a standard box-style cabinet
